Automation testing is a software testing technique that uses automated tools to execute tests, compare actual and expected results, and generate reports. Automation testing aims to increase the speed and efficiency of the testing process while improving result accuracy and reliability.

To initiate automation, whether on a private or public node server, you must replace the existing openUI5112027 within the closedmodules directory with the new openUI5112027. Additionally, ensure the sap-ui-version.json file is copied into closedmodules. Following these steps, if operating on a private node, restart the server and proceed with re-registration.

WDIO is a hugely popular E2E testing framework for Web Applications. This also includes hybrid apps. It can drive a real browser and simulate a user interacting with the app. WDIO can work with apps that use any web framework but there are certain advantages if the testing framework integrates with the web framework. If this is the case, the tests could be much simpler to write and mainly, much more reliable. Reliability is of paramount importance for E2E tests that typically struggle with flakiness so any improvement can have significant effect on the TCO of testing process

documents.t: By following the above instructions, you will ensure that dialogs opened using the KloController.openDialog API are closed consistently and correctly with the KloController.closeDialog API. This approach helps avoid potential issues and improves the stability and maintainability of the application.
Screenshot
Screenshot

Dialogs opened via the KloController.openDialog API should be closed using the KloController.closeDialog API, not the sap.m.Dialog's close method. The sap.m.Dialog's close method should only be used when the dialog was opened via the sap.m.Dialog.open() method.

It has been noted that some applications are using the sap.m.Dialog's close method to close dialogs that were opened via the KloController.openDialog API. This can result in inconsistencies and potential issues. To maintain uniformity and prevent problems, it is essential that the KloController.closeDialog API is used to close dialogs opened by the KloController.openDialog API.

Row wise authorization is a security feature provided by a framework with which access to entity data can be restricted to selective row items on user level. By default, when a simple select query is fired on any entity, it returns all data that is present in the entity. But, by enabling and configuring row wise authorization on an entity, the list of records accessible to any user can be controlled using access tokens.

documents.t: API Services Screen Date of Issue: 28.12.2023 Target Audience: Application Developer Prepared by: Nayan Adhikary Platform Version: 6.0 A User Manual for application creation, knowledge and work reference.
API Services are special application endpoints, that can be used to access application custom services. These can be created for an app and configured as required.

Basics of HTTP request, BOL logics. Latest version is to be assigned for accessing this application. The flavor(App), in which the App service will be created, needs to be build. app_services app needs to be assigned

Step 1: App Selection Process As you have already opened the App Service Screen, click the option to select assigned Apps. Only writable apps are editable. Step 2: Make data editable To edit the data present click on the Edit button on the top right side of the screen. Step 3: Add an app service Fill in the Apsr_id and method_type In case you submit without filling in the fields. The method type must be either “GET” or “POST”. Step 4: Value Help to be provided Value Help is provided for both type and method_type. Type Method type parameters(key-value pair/ any parameters) Step 5: Authorization process Authorization shows whether one has permission to access the app from an authorised user or anyone. Yes- The call is authorized based on a valid user, the user has access to the app. No - The call is unauthorized and can be accessed by anyone. Confirmation dialog is given. When cancelled, it returns to its original state. If confirmed, changes authorization and changes the state too.
documents.s: API Services — Procedure to work on App Service
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/API Services/Procedure to work on App Service

documents.t: Step 6: Save the entire process Saves the changes. Step 7: To cancel the process In case you want to cancel the changes you have made. When pressed cancel, a Confirmation dialog is shown if there are changes. If pressed OK, it reverts the unsaved changes. Step 8: Selecting a different App without saving When the changes are unsaved and you try to select a different app, there will be a confirmation dialog which will confirm your proceeding. If cancelled, it stays on the same Page. If confirmed, it goes to the selected app. Doesn’t save the changes made. Step 9: Deleting selected app_services Selected will be deleted if confirmed. If cancelled after deleting, without saving, changes back to before saving. Step 10: Navigating Back without saving If cancelled, revert the changes to the last save and navigate back. If pressed OK, saves the changes and then navigates. To cancel the navigation, when on the confirmation, press esc button.
documents.s: API Services — Procedure to work on App Service
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/API Services/Procedure to work on App Service

documents.t: Application URLs support version-based access using the following format: https://<domain>/appservice/<landscape>/<flavor>_<version>/<api_id> where <version> follows the format: <major>-<minor>-<patch> When resolving an application version: The specified major and minor versions are honored. The system automatically resolves the request to the latest available patch version within the specified major.minor version. Example​ Available versions: 7-0-1 7-0-5 7-0-20 Request: /appservice/prod/mobile_7-0-1/api123 Resolved Version: 7-0-20 Similarly, if versions 8-1-3, 8-1-10, and 8-2-5 are available: Request: /appservice/prod/mobile_8-1-3/api123 Resolved Version: 8-1-10 This behavior ensures that consumers automatically receive the latest available patch fixes and improvements within the requested major.minor release stream without requiring URL updates.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/API Services/Procedure to work on App Service

documents.t: App List consists of all the internal Apps with Manager Access.
Click on any app version to open its details. App detail section allows the users to see the App status, App Network Mode, and modify the list of Parent Apps. *Only Active/Open Apps are Editable.
Note: If a flavor version is deleted and a new version of the same flavor is assigned immediately, it won't work. The user must save changes before adding the new version.
Section where users can add, remove, and change the sequence of apps (by drag and drop) as parents to the current app. Clicking on the parent app activates it, if it's assigned.
Shows Created and Modified fields along with the last Dev Build details.

Shows a popup with the options: Cancel: Stays in the Current App. Discard: Discards the changes made and sets the selected app as active. Save: Opens a dialog with saving options and keeps the user in the current app. Refer to Step 4 for the saving process.
Cancel: Doesn’t navigate. OK: Doesn’t Save the changes made and navigates back.

App overriding is a feature where the child apps inherit the features of the parent app and override their properties. This screen is used to display and highlight the overridden elements and their properties.
Date of Issue: September 2024 Version: 7.0 Prepared by: Nayan Adhikary Target Audience: Application Developers

Maintaining a proper hierarchy between app versions is crucial for accurate dependency management, for this a correct approach to establish a multi-level hierarchy is required, ensuring that dependencies are calculated correctly. To maintain the hierarchy effectively, it always starts from the top-most parent and works your way down to the bottom-most child. Example: Current Versions: A-1 (Top-most Parent) B-1 C-1 D-1 (Bottom-most Child) Correct Hierarchy: A-1 -> B-1 -> C-1 -> D-1 Note: To ensure accurate dependency management; Always maintain hierarchy from the top-most parent to the bottom-most child. This method prevents errors in dependency calculations and keeps the app structure coherent.

Step 1: Go to the menu options and select App Lifecycle and then App Dependencies. Step 2: The App Dependencies screen will open. Refer this section to know about app modifications; App Modifications.
documents.s: App Dependencies — Navigate to App Dependencies

documents.t: App Dependencies is an Admin Tool that focuses on managing the hierarchy of the applications. This tool manages the inheritance and sequence of the applications.
The account_6-0-17 or above App should be assigned to the user to access the Account Editor.
Account and app_util flavor should be assigned to the user to get to the app override screen.
documents.s: App Dependencies — Prerequisites for App Modifications

documents.t: Select the version of the app you wish to inherit and click the edit button.
Click on the “+” button and a popup will appear.

Select App from the dialog and it will be added in Parent Apps. NOTE: DEPRECATED or DISCARDED Apps won’t be shown in the list. If the selected flavor is already present in the hierarchy, addition will not be allowed, and a message toast will be displayed. Otherwise, the process will proceed as usual. Popup will be shown if an App with status other than RELEASED is selected. Press on the ADD button to add the App to the parent List (If the App is not RELEASED).

Click on the save button after making changes. A Popup will be shown for choosing the options that needs to be done after Save Select the Options provided; Apply Changes: Overridden things in the child App will revert back to the original as parent App.(Currently Blocked as it is having some issues) Publish: It will navigate to the Validate and Build Page(if Assigned/present) with the current App selected. Note: When adding or removing parent apps from the current apps, all child apps of the current ones must be updated. To ensure that all flavors are published, the "Publish" option needs to be selected. If the user does not select "Publish," a dialog will appear as shown below. If the user intends to publish, they should click "No," which will return to the previous dialog. If they prefer not to publish, they should click "Yes," and the process will proceed with generateSequence without publishing. Sequence generation is done on every save. Note: After generating sequence , build is required for the app to see the changes.

This screen can be used for; To summarize all the overridden elements along with their root elements in a tree hierarchy. To categorize the overridden elements (based on entity/page/menu etc.). To display and compare all the properties of the selected element with its parent flavor and other versions of the same flavor. To represent all the modified versions of the parent and child app and compare their element's properties. To navigate to the respective element's page.

To display the overridden data; Step 1: Go to the menu options and select App Lifecycle and then App Dependencies. App modification screen will display as shown below; Select the name of the child flavor from the flavor dropdown in the toolbar as shown below; Select the element types which need to be displayed. This App Lifecycle Events - User Guide provides a structured way for developers to handle various stages of the application's lifecycle. The AppLifeCycleEvent class contains methods that are triggered by the framework to respond to key lifecycle events such as: App start App moves to the foreground App goes into the background App close This allows an efficient and organized management of application behavior in response to above mentioned events. This is a screen that helps make changes in the settings and setting groups that are used in any application.

Note: If the developers want to make any changes to the Settings Definition Screen metadata then they will have to assign core_fw as a dependent app to the fw_settings1_1 app and then build the fw_settings1 flavor and reinitialize it. Only then any changes should be made. Also for save to work, assign is_external for fw_settings1 flavor as 1. To save any changes made on the Settings Definition user needs a shared, writable app.
Flavor: fw_settings1

Go to the menu App Settings. Click on the sub-menu named Settings Definition to open it. The Screen will be loaded initially with all the settings inside their respective Settings Group in a tree in ascending order based on their sequence value. Settings Group will also be in ascending order of their sequence values. Click on the Edit option in the upper right corner of the screen. On the toolbar of the screen, you will find the Create Group, Create Settings, Save, Delete and Cancel buttons. You can create the settings group by clicking the +Group button on the top right of the screen. It will ask the developer to provide the Settings Group ID in an input dialog. Click on the Create button in the input dialog. After creating a new Settings Group, users can see it updated in the Table Tree below. Users need to fill in the Sequence number, Title and Icon of that settings group and then click on the Save button to save the newly created settings group. All the settings groups will now be shown in ascending order of their sequence value. The developer then needs to create Settings inside the newly created settings group. To do that the user needs to select that settings group on the tree and then click on +Setting Button. It will ask for the Settings ID under Create Setting and the developer needs to provide the ID and click on the Create button. A new setting will be created inside the selected settings group. The developer needs to fill in the Title, Description, Sequence Number, Icon, Data Type, UI type, Vh ID, Default value, visible and modifiable_in and then click on Save to save all the changes. After successful save, all the settings in their respective groups will be in ascending order of their sequence value. Components Descriptions Title It's the name you want to put to identify the setting control. Description A short description of the setting element. Sequence Number This will put the setting elements according to the order of its sequence. Icon This implies an individual settings icon. Data Type It's the type of the setting, whether it's a number, an integer or a string etc. UI Type It is the type of Control that you want to render in the UI for those Settings such as Input, Slider, value Help, etc. Vh ID It is the value help ID created from bol editor on application flavor and it will be shown to the user as value help items in case the user has chosen UI type as VH. Default Value It's a pre-value that has been set for some particular setting. This is changeable according to your requirements. visible This implies who will be able to see the particular setting item. modifiable in This puts down conditions on who can see the setting items and so on. To update any details click on the edit button in the toolbar and after updating the details click on save to commit the changes. If you have updated any details and do not want it to commit then you can click on the reset button in the toolbar to set the details to the original state.

documents.t: The "replaceMap" action is utilized for incorporating additional variables that can be utilized across all files during runtime. This method proves beneficial for transmitting parameters within our functions, given that direct argument passing isn't feasible in array format. By employing this workaround, we simulate the behavior of passing arguments as done conventionally in regular functions. Note :- For the "replaceMap" action, an additional key-value pair, "data", must be included in the object. The "data" attribute is designed to store an array of objects, each representing a variable and its value that you wish to declare or store within the replaceMap. Upon repeated use of the same variables within replaceMap, it will overwrite the older values with the newly assigned ones. In the provided example, you'll notice the absence of "controlID" or "domElementId". This is because no actions were performed on any specific element; hence, the user needs to craft this function manually instead of generating it through a test recorder. Same will happen with many actions that are not performed on any elements.

documents.t: Within the closedmodules directory, establish a new folder titled klo_automation_1. Within this, create another folder dedicated to your automation, housing all requisite files needed to execute the automation. Note :- Adhering to this specific structure is crucial for the successful execution of the automation. The automation process attempts to access certain files, notably the klarion.json file located within the kloconfig folder, from your private node. Therefore, maintaining this structure ensures that the automation can correctly locate and utilize these files from their designated locations. Should you deviate from this structure, you will need to adjust the paths in conf.data.js accordingly to reflect the correct locations of your files. The files mentioned above are essential for running the automation. Let's examine each of these files individually.

Located within the kloAu directory, this file stands as the core component of the automation suite. It houses all necessary functions tasked with transforming array-formatted code into a conventional format. Since WDIO cannot interpret array formats directly, this conversion is imperative for compatibility.

This file will house all fundamental configurations necessary for the automation to operate, including user credentials, URLs, and the specific Chrome directory in which the execution should occur. baseUrl: Users must specify the URL to be accessed at the beginning of the automation process. userId: The User ID associated with the login or registration conducted on the previously mentioned URL. Password: The user's password, if applicable. desktopLoginID: For the desktop login ID, users need to supply the User ID used for logging in on their desktop. Profile_directory: Users must indicate the Chrome profile directory where they intend to run the automation. Specs: Within the Specs object, users must list the names of the specs they wish to execute, adhering to a sequential order. It's important to note that the names provided are case-sensitive. Ensure consistency in naming across all references to avoid discrepancies. NOTE :- The Spec and Data file names should be entered exactly as demonstrated in the preceding example. Additionally, the object name must remain consistent. Please remember that the names provided are case-sensitive. ReplaceMap :-This file includes all the application variables required for test cases. Variables must be declared within double dollar signs, like $variable_name$ How replaceMap Operates in Automation:​ In the array format data file, replaceMap searches for all variables declared either in conf.data.js or at runtime within the data file itself. Whenever it encounters a match, it substitutes the matched variable with the corresponding value from the object's key-value pair. Note: By default, two variables, $dateKey$ and $landscape$, are automatically created within replaceMap at runtime. These variables can also be utilized within your data file. $dateKey$: This variable holds the current date and time. It's particularly useful for generating unique names for entities and screens each time the automation runs. For instance, in the example provided, the $entityName$ variable is set to "d_autest_$dateKey$". During execution, %dateKey% is replaced with the current date and time, resulting in a unique identifier like d_autest_25_06_12_11. $landscape$: Contains the name of the landscape for which the private node was created. This value is derived from the klarion.json file, indicating the landscape's name.

This file encompasses all the scripts generated by the test recorder. Essentially, it stores the test script or code in array format that was produced. Observing the header section of the tsData variable, we find an object containing several key-value pairs. Let's explore these details further. Remark: This field allows you to summarize what the entire specs entails or outlines the actions performed by the specs. A point to remember is that this summary will also appear as the specs name in the HTML report. Reload and Login: These should always be set to true to ensure that the login process occurs every time the automation starts. Menu: Used to specify the navigation path to the desired menu. The structure follows the pattern of the menu group name, preceded by a forward slash, and then the menu name. For instance, to open the Procify Data Studio inside App Builder, the menu entry would be “App Builder/Procify Data Studio”. It's important to note that both the menu group and menu name are case-sensitive. Note: Test Spec/Data files generated from the Test Recorder will not include the menu key-value pair in the header object. Developers must manually add this information.

This file encompasses all the function declarations originally listed or created in the myUtil.js file. Additionally, it provides a designated space for declaring any function that is intended to be utilized exclusively within its corresponding data file. NOTE :- In the spec_name.spec.js file, towards the end, there's a highlighted segment shown in the accompanying image. Within the loadData function located at the bottom of this file, you must include your spec's name as a parameter. This name should precisely match the one listed under the specs section in the conf.data.js file. To ensure consistency across your files and facilitate the automation process, it's crucial to maintain identical naming conventions. Any discrepancy in naming, including variations in capitalization, will prevent the automation from initiating.

This file will contain all the functions that you want to use throughout your entire automation. We can create function in two formats here :- Normal Function​ Standard functions will adhere to the conventional coding practices of WDIO. We cannot incorporate any code snippets formatted as arrays in this context.These functions prove beneficial when dealing with non-UI5 pages, such as the registration or login pages of our servers. These functions are utilized in scenarios where there is no requirement for using replaceMap or variable replacement from a replaceMap.json file, as the standard functions do not support the replacement of variables denoted by $variable_name$ for ui5 pages. As demonstrated in the following example, neither replaceMap variables nor code formatted as arrays are employed, eliminating the need for runtime replacements. To grasp how we can manage non-UI5 pages or write code in a standard format, let's delve into the following: The $ command serves as a concise method to retrieve a single element from a webpage. addValue: This function allows adding a value to an input or textarea element identified by a specific selector. click: Executes a WebDriver click action on the chosen element. By default, this action involves scrolling to and clicking the targeted element unless otherwise specified. In the subsequent example, we demonstrate the process of selecting a password field element and verifying its presence on the screen using the isDisplayed() API. If the element is visible, we proceed to insert the user's password using addValue and subsequently click the login button. Array Format Function​ Array format functions in the context of writing code snippets in spec_name.data.js allow for the creation of reusable functions that can be called multiple times within the file. These functions are particularly useful for performing repetitive actions, especially when those actions need to be executed in a recursive manner. In such cases, defining a function within myUtil enables you to easily invoke it as many times as needed without duplicating code. Using new test recorder that generates actions in an array format, you would parse these actions and pass them to your function.By structuring your code in this way, you can efficiently manage complex sequences of actions, especially when dealing with arrays of elements or actions generated from automated tools like a test recorder. This approach promotes code reuse and simplifies the management of repetitive tasks within your tests. Understanding functions, we recognize that they can be invoked repeatedly, each time with varying parameters. Following this principle, we too employ a similar strategy. To explore how we pass parameters, we'll initially focus on utilizing these parameters within our array format code. Specifically, we leverage the replaceMap.json file, which stores the values of parameters passed to functions at runtime. Essentially, we're retrieving these parameter values stored in replaceMap.json through a function designed for our array format code. Our methodology involves declaring a variable and importing a utility function named getWordFromReplaceMap from the kloAuWdio file into our myUtil file. This function accepts a variable name (such as $entity$, which is declared in spec_name.data.js) as its parameter and returns the corresponding value from replaceMap.json at runtime.

For Node.js projects, the package.json file provides a simplified way to manage a project's metadata and dependencies. The file ensures a project always has current information about the libraries and tools it needs to work correctly.Every npm package and Node.js project has a package.json file with metadata for a project. The file resides in the root directory of every Node.js package .The package.json file contains descriptive and functional metadata about a project, such as a name, version, and dependencies. The file provides the npm package manager with various information to help identify the project and handle dependencies. To install the dependencies, transfer your most recent package.json file to your automation directory. Afterward, navigate to this directory using the command prompt and execute npm install.
The configuration file contains all necessary information to run your test suite. It’s a NodeJS module that exports a JSON. No changes should be made in that file by the developer.

WebdriverIO-plugin for wdi5. It provides the ui5-service to WebdriverIO, running tests in the browser.In case the very first called page is non-UI5 (think SAP CP CloudFoundry login), the config option skipInjectUI5OnStart can be set to true to postpone injecting wdi5 into the browser context. Consequently you have to do it later, as soon as the UI5 page to test is available. This can be done by calling injectUI5() on the wdio-ui5-service. So, the UI5 service will prove beneficial when encountering a stale element reference error during automation, preventing the automation from halting or performing unexpectedly. The stale element reference error is a WebDriver error that occurs because the referenced web element is no longer attached to the DOM.Every DOM element is represented in WebDriver by a unique identifying reference, known as a web element. The web element reference is a UUID used to execute commands targeting specific elements, such as getting an element's tag name and retrieving a property off an element. When an element is no longer attached to the DOM, i.e. it has been removed from the document or the document has changed, it is said to be stale. Staleness occurs for example when you have a web element reference and Upon navigation, all web element references to the previous document will be discarded along with the document. This will cause any subsequent interaction with the web element to fail with the stale element reference error. To overcome this ui5 service needs to be injected again in the page again. Refer to the screenshot above for more details.

To utilize the $dateKey$ variable from conf.data.js in myUtil.js or spec_name.spec.js, the conf.data.js file must be imported into the relevant file and used appropriately since replaceMap does not operate directly within normal functions; it works only in array format code snippets. Additionally, it's crucial to note that if the $dateKey$ variable is required in the first spec_name.spec.js file, it must be imported from conf.data.js. However, if it needs to be used starting from the second spec onwards, it should be imported from replaceMap.json.
documents.s: $dateKey$ variable in spec_name.specs.js and myUtil.js file

documents.t: When using variable names in getText() and getValue() actions, they should not be reused. Although it operates similarly to replaceMap, where initializing the same variable with a different value results in replacement, this principle does not apply when storing values from the screen using getText() and getValue() actions. In these cases, repeating variable names is not allowed.
documents.s: Variables values stored using getValue() and getText()

documents.t: Occasionally, due to failed automation execution or termination mid-execution, the replaceMap.json file may become empty. Consequently, attempting to run automation afterward will fail to start. To mitigate this problem, an empty object must be explicitly declared within the replaceMap.json file.

For checkboxes within a grid, the necessary wdio code is not automatically generated. To resolve this challenge, the browser.keys() APIs should be employed as a temporary fix. Leveraging keyboard actions can also help address this issue.

If users are conducting validations on a UI-created screen following a full preview, certain codes need to be made dynamic. Otherwise, the automation will not execute correctly if triggered again or under different conditions. As illustrated in the preceding image, there are several areas (e.g., 2-3 spots) where the code requires modification to ensure successful execution each time the automation runs. For instance, consider the scenario where the automation's flavor changes; without making the code dynamic, the automation would fail. Additionally, the page name appears in both the view ID and model ID sections of the code. If a new page is introduced with a different name, the automation will also fail unless the code is updated accordingly to reflect this change dynamically.
documents.s: Validation for screen created in UI

documents.t: Sometimes, as noticed, once the menu is opened during automation, the process halts in the browser and begins displaying errors in the console. The primary issue here is that the replaceMap, which is intended to substitute variables for viewID and modelID at runtime, fails to do so; instead, it retains the original values provided in the spec_name.data.js file. To update the page's viewID and modelID with the current ones, since these identifiers change with every screen navigation, the automation executes the getModelViewNamesForAutomation() function in the console. This function retrieves the current page's viewID and modelID, which are then stored in replaceMap. If a match is found, the existing viewID and modelID in the code, formatted as an array, are replaced with the current ones. After the menu is opened in automation, the code proceeds to the next segment. Occasionally, the screen remains partially open, still showing the loading state. At this point, even though the code execution has moved forward, the screen is not fully loaded. Consequently, when the automation runs the getModelViewNamesForAutomation() function in the console, it returns the modelID and viewID of the previously viewed page, not the current one, because the page is still in the process of rendering and is not yet fully visible. Because of this, replaceMap does not work in this case. To address this issue, after the menu is opened, we need to insert a code block that does not involve viewID or modelID. The only element on the screen that lacks either viewID or modelID in its code block is the Procify logo at the top.
documents.s: replaceMap does not work after menu opening sometimes

documents.t: There may be instances where a list of elements exists, and a specific item needs to be selected from it. For example, choosing the screen type of a section from a VH list. As depicted in the image below, we generate code for selecting the search screen type from the VH list. However, within the code block, no mention of 'search' is made; instead, it merely indicates the specific path or index where the search type screen resides. If the path or index of the search were to change, the automation would encounter issues at this stage. To address this issue , we've linked it with "search" such that it consistently selects the “search” screen type from the VH list, regardless of the index. Let’s see how we will do that. Upon generating the code in procify control list section , navigate to the properties tab of test recorder. There we will be able to see different properties from which we will be able to bind this element. Therefore, among the highlighted attributes, we choose the ones that can uniquely identify this element. Specifically, for this element, both the title and description can serve as distinguishing features. Lets see how we can do the binding in the code block :- In this scenario, the path within the binding path must be commented, and a new key-value pair should be introduced, specifically 'properties'. Automation testing is a software testing technique that uses automated tools to execute tests, compare actual and expected results, and generate reports. Automation testing aims to increase the speed and efficiency of the testing process while improving result accuracy and reliability.

To initiate automation, whether on a private or public node server, you must replace the existing openUI5_1_120_27 within the closedmodules directory with the new openUI5_1_120_27. Additionally, ensure the sap-ui-version.json file is copied into closedmodules. Following these steps, if operating on a private node, restart the server and proceed with re-registration.

WDIO is a hugely popular E2E testing framework for Web Applications. This also includes hybrid apps. It can drive a real browser and simulate a user interacting with the app. WDIO can work with apps that use any web framework but there are certain advantages if the testing framework integrates with the web framework. If this is the case, the tests could be much simpler to write and mainly, much more reliable. Reliability is of paramount importance for E2E tests that typically struggle with flakiness so any improvement can have significant effect on the TCO of testing process WDIO can work with any web application but lacks the awareness of the web framework that the application uses. WDI5, which is a WDIO plugin, bridges this gap and provides two key benefits, namely control locators and synchronization with the web framework. WDIO supports many types of locators - css, xpath, even plain javascript code but it lacks understanding of the UI5 controls. WDI5 exposes a browser.byControl() method that accepts a control locator and returns a proxy for the real control. Then the test can assert on the control state or even interact with the control. The second benefit is transparent but equally important – on every element interaction, WDI5 waits for UI5 rendering to complete and for the application to be completely stable.

documents.t: Use C R U D flags to control the data updation to your entity. Naming conventions to be followed. Entity name should start with d_ for Tenent dependent and tenant independent entities. t_ for transient entities. c_ for config entities. Use Validate BO on every change in entity to avoid runtime errors. Use the sort order functionality in your entity, this will eliminate sorting in each screen. Entity id should have only small letters.

Entity’s network Mode should be blank for all entities under the flavor (Flavor network mode will be used by default). Network mode can only be overridden on exceptional cases. Example : In Offline App only one page is online.

Naming conventions to be followed for property id’s. Property id should start with t_ for transient type properties. c_ for calculated type properties. Make sure that every property details are filled properly, this will boost the development. Mandatory: On create/update of the records from any screen, klobase will validate mandatory fields. Fuzzy: If the fields marked with fuzzy exist on the screen, klobase will auto add them for fuzzy search criteria Eg: description / short text / name of the customer. Default Value : On create system will auto populate these fields with the default values Eg: Priority, -- If any logic to identify the default value then it should be added in <entity name > .TS file. VH: Make sure the VH field is not blank wherever VH help can be determined. Text ID: Add a text ID and maintain the text in the language editor, avoid direct text / label in these fields. Entity Property should have only small letters. Note : In case a user wants to change the property type of any property, they have to re-add the same property in their screen metadata using Page Builder (wherever applicable) from their transnode for reflecting the changes.

Don’t create properties for system fields like s_modified_on, s_created_by, s_created_on. Instead enable created fields flag to use inbuilt system properties. Don’t create / use new element ids if the same property is created under any other entity Example : Order id in order header and order item can share same element id Use the “Extend from” option if the existing property type can be used with minor changes like label changes or mandatory change.
Naming conventions need to be followed for the id series id’s. Id should starts with id_ Id Series should have only small letters.

Naming conventions need to be followed for relation id’s. Relation name should start with pr_ for primary relation r_ for associated relation Primary Relations: Always bundle your Bo with all children entities so that handling the data update messages would be easier. Non Primary Relations: Always specify all the secondary relations also to avoid fetching data directly with queries. You can use relation fetch instead. Entity Relations should have only small letters.
Always maintain the object group to group the types and the same can be used in default filters based on users. Object types should always be binded with role and role_roll_up (for vienable).

Network Mode / DB selection should be blank for all queries under the flavor. Flavor network mode will be used by default. It can be overridden only for exceptional cases. Example: In offline apps only 1 screen is online. Create a query only if entity query is not sufficient for the use case. Use a modeled query as it is independent of DBMS. Naming conventions need to be followed for query id’s. The query should have only small letters. Query id should starts with q_
Don’t use native query as it is dependent on the DBMS. Use it only for special use cases. Don't use different id's for query properties. Use the id same as entity property for easy trace.

Use rules for endpoint resolvers. Always use Ts files as exit handler for better readability and maintenance. Rules should have only small letters. Naming conventions need to be followed for rules subscriptions. Should starts with d2k_ for Endpoint / Device to Klarion Server clnt_ for Endpoint / Device to Klarion Server - Always on client srvr_ for Endpoint / Device to server / Client - NETWORK CONTEXT SWITCH ncs_ for Endpoint / Device to Server / client - network context switch k2d_ for Klarion Server to Klarion Offline Server k2k_ for Klarion Server to Klarion Server e2k _ for Legacy to Klarion Server
Avoid using rules for create / update scenarios, we can make use of <entity_name>.ts files to handle the same. Use onCreate & onUpdate hook methods of the <entity_name>.ts

Naming conventions need to be followed for value help id’s. Vh id should start with vht_ for vh transactional vhq_ for query vhsq_ for saved query vhc_ for config Value Help should have only small letters.
Date of Issue: March 2023 Version: 7.0 Target Audience: Application Development Trainees
Naming convention needs to be followed for page id’s. Page id should start with p_ Example : p_orders, p_notification The page should have only small letters.
Naming convention needs to be followed for page Layout id’s Page Layout ids should start with Pl_ Example: pl_desktop, pl_mobile Page Layout should have only small letters.
Naming convention needs to be followed for page Area id’s Page Area ids should start with pa_ Example: pa_no_header_detail. Page Area should have only small letters.
Naming convention needs to be followed for section id’s Section ids should start with s_ Example : s_no_header_list The section should have only small letters.
Naming convention needs to be followed for embedded sections Embedded section id’s should start with es_ The Embedded Section should have only small letters.
Only use kloAction control as action buttons.

Naming conventions should be followed for transNode’s Transnode name should end with _detail for entity type _list for entityset type _query for query type _other for other type TransNode should have only small letters.
Use kloInput control for F4 - By providing vh_type as f4. Combobox - By providing vh_type as combobox. Autocomplete - By providing vh_type as autocomplete. Input - By providing vh_type as none.
Don’t change the control’s class unless it is necessary.

Only UI related logics should be written in controller file Example: formatter functions, navigation function. public navToDetail(oEvent){ this.navToByEventss(oEvent,'s_header_detail'); } Create a variable only if it is necessary While declaring a variable in Ts file make sure to maintain the type of the variable Example: let isValidItem: boolean = true; let item:KloEntitySet<d_order_item> = this.tm.getTN("/item").getData();

Model properties should not be altered in the controller file(can be done in that <entity_name>.ts file). Only in case of any special scenario it is allowed. Example: Functions like setting property based on another property change should be ignored, it should be written in entity file setter. Nested functions should not be used in the controller file. Don’t use deprecated API.

Only business logic functions should be written inside the entity file. Example: The name property needs to be changed when first_name or last_name is getting changed public set firstName(new_value:string){ if(new_value == this.firstName) return; this.name = new_value+" "+this.lastName; this.s("firstName",new_value,"string",false,false); }
UI logic should not be written inside an entity file. Don’t use deprecated API.

Getter functions​ public get name():string{ return this.Firstname +" "+this.lastName; } Setter functions:​ public set firstName(new_value:string){ if(new_value == this.firstName) return; this.name = new_value+" "+this.lastName; this.s("firstName",new_value,"string",false,false); } onValidate functions:​ public async OnValidate(){ if(this.priority === "1"){ this.errors.push(new ValidationError(this,"priority","11","Priority should not be High")); } } onDelete​ onDelete method will be called once the entity is deleted. public onDelete():Promise<any>{ console.log("on deletion of entity"); return; } onAfterCreate​ onAfterCreate method will be called once the new entity is created. public onAfterCreate():Promise<any>{ console.log("on creating a new entity"); return; }

If CSS files are committed in a parent flavor, it's important to commit the same files in child flavors to maintain consistency and avoid discrepancies. If any updates or bug fixes are made to the CSS in the parent flavor, the child flavors will benefit from those updates if they share the same files.If a child flavor doesn't have the CSS files, it might result in missing or incorrect styling due to the lack of inherited rules.

A UX (User Experience) guideline refers to a set of best practices, principles, and rules designed to enhance the overall experience users have when interacting with a product or application. These guidelines help ensure that they are easy to use, intuitive, and meet the needs of the user. In UX design, CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) plays a crucial role in shaping the visual presentation and overall design of a product or application. While UX focuses on the overall experience and usability, CSS ensures that the design is visually appealing, consistent, and easy to navigate, which directly affects how users interact with the product. Message box is a dialog box or pop-up that displays important information to users.They often contain a title, a message, and buttons for users to acknowledge or take further action.Buttons will be of affirmative(primary button) and dismissive(secondary button).​ AffirmativeButton(emphasized ) - Has white text on a blue background.​ Example: "Yes," "Approve," "Confirm", etc. Dismissive Button( negative)- Has Blue text on a white background.​ Example: "No," "Reject," "Cancel", etc. 1. Success Message:​ The "Success" message, displayed with a green color to indicate positive completion, provides users with immediate confirmation that their action was successful. For example, "Project 1234567 was created and assigned to team ABC." This message reassures users that the action has been processed correctly, with the green color highlighting the positive outcome. The primary button has white text on a blue background. 2. Warning Message:​ The "Warning" message, displayed with an orange color, is designed to catch attention without indicating an error. For example, "The project schedule was last updated over a year ago." This message alerts users to potential issues, such as outdated information, providing a gentle reminder to review or update without suggesting a critical failure. The orange color effectively signals caution while maintaining a non-critical tone. The primary button has white text on a blue background.Secondary button has an inverted primary button. 3. Standard Error Message:​ Title: Error, the "Error" message is displayed with a red color to indicate a problem. For example, "Select a team in the 'Development' area. 'Marketing' isn't assigned to this area." It will persist until the user takes action, such as clicking to dismiss or retrying the action. The red color signals an issue that requires attention and correction. 4.Data loss Message:​ Title: Save? The "Data Loss" message box is displayed with an orange line to alert users about the potential loss of data. For example, "Please save or discard the modified data.." The message will persist until the user takes action, such as confirming or canceling the action. The color and message emphasize the importance of saving before proceeding to prevent losing valuable information. 5. Standard Confirmation Message:​ Title: Confirmation,the "Approve purchase order?" message is displayed with a grey color to indicate a neutral confirmation.​ For example, "Approve purchase order 12345?" .​ It will persist until the user takes action, such as clicking "OK" to confirm or "Cancel" to dismiss. The grey color signals a non-urgent action that requires the user's approval.​ 6. Information Message: The "Information" message is displayed with a grey color to indicate a neutral, non-urgent notification. For example, "This Message Box has responsive paddings which will adjust based on its content width!" It will persist until the user dismisses it. The grey color signals that this is an informational message without requiring immediate action. 7. Sequential execution process Title: “Import status ” Line Color: Grey/Light green (indicating a neutral confirmation) Text Message: Shown below; Description: This message provides a visual representation of the sequential execution process. The status is displayed with a grey or light green line, indicating neutral confirmation. As each step of the process is completed, points are ticked off one by one, showing the progress of the import status. 8. Multiple warnings (Validation case) The "Validation Warning" message is displayed with an orange color to indicate issues that need attention. For example, "Control will not be rendered/control is not in use…..)" This message will persist until the user addresses the validation issues, ensuring necessary corrections are made. The orange color highlights that the user must take action to proceed. 9.Multiple Error Messages Multiple error messages are displayed with a white background and grey text to indicate issues that need immediate attention. For example, "Value for Mandatory field missing" These messages persist until the user resolves the errors, with each issue clearly outlined.

Position of Buttons: Cancel Button: Always placed on the right side of the dialog box or message popup to follow established UI conventions. This button should allow the user to exit or cancel the action. Affirmative Action Button(emphasized): The action button (such as Save, Yes, or Confirm) should be highlighted (typically in a blue or green color) to make it prominent and easily accessible to the user. This button should be placed on the left side, preceding the Cancel button.

Color Meaning Example Green Success “Project 1234567 was created and assigned to team ABC.” Red Error “Select a team in the “Development” area. “Marketing” isn't assigned to this area” Orange Warning “The project schedule was last updated over a year ago.” Grey Confirmation “Approve purchase order 12345?” Grey Neutral/Information “This Message Box has responsive paddings which will adjust based on its content width!” Grey/Light green sequential execution process "Import Status" Text Message: [✔] Step 1: Data Validation [✔] Step 2: File Upload [✔] Step 3: Data Processing [✔] Step 4: Finalizing Import [✔] Step 5: Import Complete
In App Management, for the App, Developer AI needs to be enabled

Row-Wise Authorization Saved Query / Initial Sync Framework Offline Related Features Entity Indexing Sort Order Note: As Developer AI uses Artificial Intelligence to interpret business requirements, the generated application may not always be complete or entirely accurate. The quality of the generated output depends on the clarity and completeness of the provided BRD or BBP. It is recommended to perform a thorough functional and technical review before deploying the application.

Entities After the application is generated, all the business entities created by Developer AI are automatically available in the Data Studio. These entities form the core data model of the generated application and can be reviewed and further configured as needed. The left navigation panel displays the list of all generated entities. Selecting an entity opens its complete configuration, where you can review its properties, relationships, business rules, workflows, access control, and other metadata. Note: If the generated entities are not immediately visible in the Data Studio, refresh the application or browser. The entities will be displayed once the latest metadata is loaded. Screens Developer AI automatically generates the required application pages based on the uploaded BRD/BBP. These pages provide the user interface for interacting with the generated business entities and application features. The generated pages are available in the Page Builder and can be reviewed, customized, or enhanced using the standard Procify page designer. In the example shown, Developer AI has generated the following pages: p_homepage_001 – The application's landing page that provides users with the initial view after logging in. p_dashboard_001 – Displays the application's dashboard, providing a consolidated view of key information, widgets, and business insights. p_delivery_mgmt – The Delivery Management page used to create, view, update, and manage delivery-related transactions. Role & Users The roles and users generated by Developer AI can be viewed from the Roles & Users section under the Details tab of the generated application in App Management. This section allows you to review the user roles and user assignments created for the application. Homepage Log in using one of the users created in the Roles & Users section. After successful login, the application opens the Homepage generated by Developer AI. The homepage displayed corresponds to the configuration defined in the Homepage component during the application generation process. It serves as the application's landing page and provides users with quick access to the generated modules, dashboards, and navigation menus based on their assigned role and permissions. Dashboard Developer AI automatically generates the application dashboard based on the requirements defined in the uploaded BRD or BBP. The generated dashboard provides users with a consolidated view of key business information, metrics, and navigation components relevant to the application. It is designed to offer quick access to important data and frequently used features immediately after login. The dashboard created by Developer AI can be accessed from the Dashboard menu within the generated application and can be further customized using the standard Procify dashboard designer to meet specific business requirements. Note: The layout, widgets, and overall design of the generated dashboard are determined by Developer AI based on its analysis of the uploaded BBP or BRD. Dashboard generation is AI-driven, and users cannot control or define the dashboard layout by providing screenshots or sample designs. To influence the generated dashboard, include clear and detailed dashboard requirements within the BBP or BRD. Menu Developer AI automatically generates the application's navigation menu based on the modules, screens, and user workflows defined in the uploaded BRD or BBP. The generated menu provides users with organized navigation to access the application's features. Menu items are created based on the business requirements and are assigned appropriate access according to the generated user roles and permissions. In the example shown, Developer AI has generated the following menu items: Home – The default landing page that provides users with quick access to the application. My Deliveries – A module for managing and viewing delivery-related transactions. Dashboard – Provides access to the application's dashboard, displaying key business insights and summary information.

When a user provides a business requirement through a prompt, Developer AI performs the following activities: Requirement Understanding Interprets the user's business requirement using Natural Language Processing (NLP). Identifies the business objective, workflows, business entities, users, and relationships. Extracts key functional and data requirements from the provided description. Business Analysis Converts the natural language requirement into structured business insights. Identifies business processes, modules, and system interactions. Determines the application's functional scope and required components. Data Model Generation Analyzes the business entities involved. Identifies attributes, primary keys, foreign keys, and relationships. Generates a normalized data model suitable for the application. **Diagram Generation ** Based on the analyzed requirements, Developer AI automatically generates design artifacts such as: Entity Relationship (ER) Diagram Data Relationship Diagrams Business Process Flow Diagrams Other architecture and visualization diagrams required for application planning These diagrams provide a clear visual representation of the application's structure before development begins. Entity Creation Creates all required business entities. Defines fields, data types, validations, constraints, and relationships. Configures entities according to Procify platform standards. **Screen Generation ** Developer AI automatically generates the application's user interface, including: Data Entry Screens List/Grid Views Detail Pages Forms Navigation structure The generated screens are mapped directly to the underlying business entities and workflows. **Dashboard Generation ** Based on the application's business context, Developer AI creates dashboards containing: Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) Charts and Graphs Summary Cards Business Metrics Data Visualizations These dashboards provide users with meaningful insights into their business data from the outset. **Application Foundation Creation ** After generating the business model, entities, screens, and dashboards, Developer AI produces the initial application structure within the Procify platform. This foundation serves as the starting point for further customization, refinement, and deployment.

documents.t: Developer AI is an enhancement to the Procify Low-Code/No-Code Platform that enables users to build enterprise applications by describing their requirements in natural language. Instead of manually configuring application components, users can generate applications through a single prompt, significantly accelerating the application development process.

We can access Developer AI from chatbot, the chatbot Icon is preset beside notification icon, in Homepage header Note: The chatbot icon is displayed only when Developer AI is enabled for the current landscape. If Developer AI is not enabled, the chatbot icon will not be visible. After click on this chatbot Icon, it will open the chatbot, from there to use the Developer AI, click on “Advanced Mode “ option, which will open the screen for using Developer AI

The Upload Business Requirement Document screen is the first step in the Developer AI application generation workflow. In this step, users select the target application, review the available AI token quota, and upload the Business Requirement Document (BRD) or Business Blueprint (BBP) that Developer AI will analyze to generate the application. Select Application​ The Select Application dropdown displays all applications, select application with Developer AI enabled the selected application acts as the target application where Developer AI will generate all the required components. All AI-generated artifacts, such as entities, screens, dashboards, workflows, and configurations, are created within the selected application. Ensure the correct application is selected before proceeding with document upload. Note :- 1. Developer AI not Enabled for Application If Developer AI is not enabled for the selected Application, It will show warning that Developer AI is not enabled for that application 2. Developer AI server is not available If the Developer AI Server is not running, a dialog will be displayed with the message: “Developer AI server is currently unavailable. Kindly contact the Administration team.” 3. BBP Build is triggered when other BBP build is in-progress in the same application If Build is triggered in the same application when other BBP Build is in-progress in the same application, then also the warning will come showing the BBP Build is already in progress Token Quota​ The Token Quota section displays the AI token consumption details for the selected user. A token represents a unit of text processed by the AI model. Every analysis performed on a BRD or BBP consumes tokens. The Token Quota panel provides the following information: Tokens Used – Total number of tokens consumed by Developer AI. Total Token Allocation – Maximum tokens allocated to the application. Remaining Tokens – Tokens still available for future AI operations. Usage Percentage – Visual progress bar showing the percentage of the allocated quota that has been consumed. Token Units​ Developer AI displays large token counts using abbreviated units: Unit Meaning Example K Thousand (1,000) 250K = 250,000 tokens M Million (1,000,000) 2.0M = 2,000,000 tokens Example If the Token Quota displays: 2.0M / 26.5M tokens 7% Used 24.5M Remaining It means: A total of 26.5 million tokens have been allocated. 2.0 million tokens have already been consumed. 24.5 million tokens are still available. Approximately 7% of the total token allocation has been utilized. Generate BBP​ The Generate BBP feature enables users to generate a Business Blueprint (BBP) by simply describing their application requirements in natural language. Instead of manually preparing a detailed BBP document, users can provide a high-level business description, and Developer AI automatically transforms it into a structured Business Blueprint. Upload BRD / BBP Document​ Once the application has been selected, upload the project documentation for analysis. Developer AI supports the following documents: Business Requirement Document (BRD) Business Blueprint (BBP) The document can be uploaded by: Dragging and dropping the file into the upload area. Selecting the file from the local system. Once the document is uploaded, Developer AI begins analyzing its contents to understand the business requirements and extract key information required to build the application. During this process, Developer AI identifies and generates: Business entities Functional requirements User roles Application screens Menu structure Business workflows Notifications Schedulers Dashboard requirements Homepage configuration Relationships between business objects The extracted information is then used to automatically generate the initial application structure within the selected Procify application. Preparing a BBP for Developer AI​ Developer AI expects the Business Blueprint (BBP) to follow a predefined structure for accurate analysis and application generation. If your existing BBP is not already in this format, it must be converted before uploading. To prepare a Developer AI-compatible BBP: Ensure you have the existing Business Blueprint (BBP) for your project. Refer to the Developer AI BBP Conversion Prompt document (Prompt). Upload both: Your existing BBP. The Developer AI BBP Conversion Prompt. Submit both documents to Claude for processing. The conversion prompt has been specifically designed and validated for Claude, and it is recommended not to use other AI models for this conversion. Claude will generate a new BBP that conforms to the standardized format required by Developer AI. Review the generated BBP to verify that the business requirements have been accurately converted. Upload the converted BBP using the Upload Business Requirement Document section to continue the application generation process. Once uploaded, Developer AI will analyze the standardized BBP and generate the application's foundational components, including entities, screens, dashboards, workflows, configurations, and other required artifacts.

The Analyze & Review tab is the second step in the Developer AI application generation workflow. In this stage, Developer AI processes the uploaded BRD or BBP and extracts all the business information required to build the application. The purpose of this step is to validate that the uploaded document has been successfully analyzed before proceeding with application generation. Once the document analysis is completed successfully and the extracted summary has been reviewed, click Open Dashboard to proceed to the detailed review screen. The Open Dashboard button opens the Review Extracted Information dashboard, where users can: Review all extracted business components in detail. Verify entities, screens, functional requirements, user roles, notifications, schedulers, menu access, and homepage configuration. Modify, add, or remove extracted items as required. Validate the extracted information before proceeding to the Execution Plan stage. Review Extracted Information​ This section provides categorized access to all the information extracted from the uploaded BRD or BBP. Each category displays the number of items identified during the analysis, allowing users to review every component before proceeding with application generation. The available categories include: Entities – Displays the entities extracted from the document. Screens – Lists the application screens identified during analysis. Schedulers – Displays scheduled jobs or background processes. Functional Requirements – Shows the extracted business requirements. Notifications – Lists notification and alert configurations. User Roles – Displays user roles identified for role-based access control. Menu Access – Shows the application's navigation menu structure. Homepage – Displays the extracted homepage configuration. Out of Scope – Lists requirements identified as outside the application's scope. AI Visualize – Provides AI-generated visual representations of the extracted business information. Ask BBP – An AI-powered assistant that answers questions related to the uploaded BBP. Selecting a category displays its corresponding details in the main content area for review. Note: At present, manual addition, modification, or deletion of extracted components is not supported. The entities, screens, functional requirements, user roles, and other components displayed on this screen are generated by Developer AI based on the uploaded BRD or BBP and are used as the foundation for application generation. Users can review the extracted information before proceeding to the next step.

Developer AI provides an option to export the extracted entity information for offline review or integration. Export to JSON​ The Export to JSON button downloads the extracted entity metadata in JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) format. The exported file contains structured information such as: Entity details Attributes Relationships Entity types Associated metadata The JSON format can be used for documentation, integration with external systems, or further processing. Export to TXT​ The Export to TXT option is currently not supported. Although the option is visible in the interface, exporting the extracted information in TXT format is not available in the current release and will be supported in a future version.

The Re-Analyze button allows users to run the document analysis again if changes have been made to the uploaded BRD or BBP, or if the extracted results need to be refreshed. When clicked, Developer AI: Reprocesses the uploaded document. Extracts the latest business requirements and application components. Updates the extracted entities, screens, functional requirements, user roles, notifications, menu access, and other information.

The Mark All Review Completed button confirms that the extracted information has been reviewed and approved. Selecting this option indicates that: The extracted entities have been verified. Screens and functional requirements have been reviewed. User roles, menu access, homepage configuration, and other extracted components have been validated. The application is ready to proceed to the next stage. Note: Marking the review as complete is mandatory before proceeding. If this step is not completed, an alert message will appear when you attempt to continue, prompting you to mark all reviews as completed before moving to the next stage.

The Execution Plan button navigates to the next step in the Developer AI workflow. After the review is completed, clicking Execution Plan opens the Execution Plan screen, where Developer AI displays the sequence of activities required to generate the application. The Execution Plan provides an overview of: Components to be generated. Order of execution. This serves as the final review before Developer AI begins generating the application.

The Refine BBP with AI feature is designed to allow users to improve or modify the extracted Business Blueprint (BBP) using natural language instructions before proceeding with application generation. This option can be accessed by clicking the ✨ (AI Refine) button available on the Review Extracted Information screen.

Click the ✨ (AI Refine) button. The Refine BBP with AI dialog is displayed. What should AI change? text box, enter the required modifications or enhancements in natural language. Examples: Tighten the module scope. Add missing approval rules. Correct notification triggers. Add a new business entity. Update the workflow for order approval. Click Apply AI Changes. Developer AI is designed to analyze the provided instructions and update the extracted BBP accordingly. The refined information would then be reflected in the extracted components for further review before proceeding with application generation. Note: The Refine BBP with AI feature is currently not supported in the current release. Although the option is available in the interface, AI-based refinement of the extracted BBP is not yet functional and will be supported in a future release.

After clicking Execution Plan, the Review BBP Changes Before Build dialog is displayed. This screen provides a final summary of the extracted Business Blueprint (BBP) before the application build process begins. The summary displays the number of: Existing in BBP – Components that were identified from the uploaded BRD or BBP. Added – New components that have been added during the review process. Updated – Components that have been modified before execution. The dialog also lists all the extracted application components, such as: Entities Screens Functional Requirements Notifications User Roles Other extracted artifacts This allows users to perform a final verification of the application metadata before proceeding with the build. Available Options Compare AI Changes – Displays a comparison between the original extracted information and any AI-generated changes (if applicable). Back to Review – Returns to the Review Extracted Information screen to make further changes or validations. Proceed to Execution Plan – Confirms the review and navigates to the Execution Plan screen, where the application generation workflow is initiated.

After clicking Proceed to Execution Plan, the Execution Selection screen is displayed. This screen allows users to review all extracted components and select the items that should be included in the application generation process. A summary at the top of the screen displays the total number of extracted components, including: Entities UI Screens Schedulers Workflows Notifications User Roles Menu Access Homepage Each category shows the number of items identified from the uploaded BRD or BBP.

The lower section displays the extracted components grouped by category. Each item is accompanied by a checkbox, allowing users to choose whether it should be included in the application build. Users can: Review the extracted entities and screens. Select or deselect individual components. Use the Select All option to include all available components for generation. Only the selected components will be considered during the application generation process.

After reviewing and selecting the required components, click Execute to start the application generation process. Developer AI begins generating the selected application components within the chosen Procify application. This includes creating the selected entities, screens, workflows, notifications, user roles, menu access, homepage configuration, and other supported artifacts. Note: Ensure that all required components are selected before clicking Execute, as only the selected items will be included in the application generation process.

After clicking Execute, the Execution Progress screen is displayed. This screen tracks the progress of the application generation process and shows the status of each component being created. To begin generating the application, click Build Application.

The Build Application button initiates the application generation process based on the components selected in the Execution Plan. During the build process, Developer AI automatically creates and configures the selected application components, including: Business entities UI screens Value Helps Sample data Application roles Notifications Business rules Menus Homepage configuration Permissions Other supported application artifacts

As the build progresses, the Execution Progress section displays the status of each component. Each component is marked with one of the following statuses: In Progress – The component is currently being generated. Completed – The component has been successfully created. The progress cards provide a quick overview of the build status for each application component.

The Execution Log records every step performed during the application generation process. The log includes information such as: Analysis completion Entity creation Screen generation Business rule creation Sample data insertion Role creation Menu generation Homepage configuration Permission assignment Any warnings or errors encountered during the build The execution log helps users monitor the build process and troubleshoot issues if required.

When all selected components have been generated successfully, the status changes to Build Completed. A confirmation message indicates that the application has been successfully created within the selected Procify application. Users can then click Continue to proceed to the next step in the Developer AI workflow. Note :- Build Queue Notification When a BBP build is triggered for an application while another BBP build is already in progress for a different application, the new build request is not started immediately. Instead, it is automatically placed in a system-wide queue and will begin execution once the currently running build is completed. Build Already in Progress If a BBP build is triggered for an application that already has an active build in progress, Developer AI does not start a new build for the same application. Instead, it notifies the user that a build is already running and provides an option to view the current build progress. Click Yes, Show Progress to open the ongoing build progress screen, or click Cancel to close the notification

This step will allow users to configure application settings, assign users and roles, manage permissions, customize branding, and define deployment-related configurations before publishing the application.
This step will allow users to validate the generated application, perform publish readiness checks, and publish the application to the target environment.
This step will allow users to generate AI-powered test cases and execute automated Playwright tests to validate the generated application.
This step will allow users to generate AI-powered technical documentation, user guides, configuration guides, and downloadable project documentation for the generated application.
This step will allow users to review the final application generation summary, verify the completed workflow, and conclude the Developer AI application generation process.

Developer AI is an AI-powered application development capability built on top of the Procify Low-Code/No-Code Platform. It transforms business requirements, provided in natural language, into a structured application design and automatically generates the foundational components required to build an enterprise application. Rather than requiring users to manually analyze requirements, design data models, create user interfaces, and configure application components, Developer AI automates these activities using artificial intelligence. This significantly reduces the time and effort involved in the initial stages of application development while ensuring consistency and alignment with business requirements.

Developer AI is designed to simplify and accelerate enterprise application development by leveraging Artificial Intelligence. It minimizes manual effort in the initial stages of development and enables organizations to transform business ideas into functional applications more efficiently.

This document explains about the various types of events associated with the page area of type ‘Dialog’ and their implementation.
This event can be used to trigger a user defined function after the dialog box has closed. One can refer to this documentation for further details : OpenUI5 After Close Documentation.
In the events tab of Dialog config, select the afterClose event and provide the name of the user defined function. Write the application logic in your controller file.
This event can be used to trigger a user defined function after the dialog box has opened. One can refer to this documentation for further details : OpenUI5 After Open Documentation.
In the events tab of Dialog config, select the afterOpen event and provide the name of the user defined function. Write the application logic in your controller file.
This event can be used to trigger a user defined function before the dialog box has closed. One can refer to this documentation for further details : OpenUI5 Before Close Documentation.
In the events tab of Dialog config, select the beforeClose event and provide the name of the user defined function. Write the application logic in your controller file.
This event can be used to trigger a user defined function before the dialog box has opened. One can refer to this documentation for further details : OpenUI5 Before Open Documentation.
In the events tab of Dialog config, select the beforeOpen event and provide the name of the user defined function. Write the application logic in your controller file.
This event can be used to override the default escape handler function on the press of escape button on the keyboard provided by sap by providing a user defined function.

In the events tab of Dialog config, select the escapeHandler event and provide the name of the user defined function. Write the application logic in your controller file. When the event is triggered, the dialog’s promise object is passed as a functional parameter. It contains two properties: resolve(): This is the dialog promise’s resolve function that can be used to resolve the dialog’s promise on close by pressing the escape button on the keyboard. reject(): This is the dialog promise’s reject function that can be used to reject the dialog’s promise on close by pressing the escape button on the keyboard. Note: Application developers can manually close the dialog by either getting the dialog instance using the getActiveControlById()function or by resolving the dialogs promise.
