This is a screen in the KloTouch application that helps the users search for the queries that they face while using the application with detailed answers. This is used to edit and create question-answers and groups in an optimised way which will benefit the ultimate consumers while using the application.
faqs_editor_1 flavor should be assigned to the User.

1. Go to the FAQs Editor menu and click on the sub-menu named FAQs Editor to open it. A screen will initially load with the FAQ Groups based on their sequence in ascending order. Note: Now the button is visible at the screen title toolbar. On click of the Procify logo, the screen title toolbar will collapse resulting in the buttons not being visible. 2. Users can search for the FAQs based on their Group Title, Question, Key ID and Key Description. Users need to enter the relevant texts and click on the OK button to perform the search. Group Title: This denotes the title under which one will find their relevant queries. Eg: If a user has a query related to Work Order, they can search for it under that very group. Questions: This denotes any search by directly writing the question on the search bar. Key ID: Key ID helps us get the element which we want. Each Flavor will be associated with one or more keys and based upon those keys, groups will be loaded for that flavor. Each key can be used in multiple flavors. Key Description: It is a relevant and memorable description that we put for the key ID. 3. Users can clear the search criteria by clicking on the cross button in the search bar. 4. Users can expand any group to see the list of questions associated with that group by clicking on the dropdown. 5. Users can click on the add button beside the search bar to create a new group. After clicking on the button, a popup will appear and the user needs to select a key to which this group will be associated. Note: These Keys are created and maintained in the Account Console. In case you do not find the key you are looking for, kindly go to the Account Console and create the relevant key. 6. Users then need to select a key and then click on the Create button. Users will be navigated to the detail section where they have to fill in the group title (mandatory), sequence, and icon and then click on the Save button. 7. Users can also edit the group details by clicking on the Edit button on the right side of that particular Group Title. 8. Users can then update the group details and then click on the Save button again. 9. Users can delete a group by clicking on the delete button on the right side of that particular group title. Upon clicking it will ask the user for confirmation. On giving the delete confirmation it will delete the group along with its entire associated question. 10. Users can create a new question inside a group by clicking on the add button at the right side of that particular group title. 11. Users then need to fill in the device type (mandatory), sequence, Question Title (mandatory) and answer and then click on the Save button. By default, the language will be set to English. 12. Users can edit a question by clicking on that particular question link. Users then need to make the changes and click on the Save button. 13. Users can also delete a question by clicking on the delete button on the right side of that particular Question Title. It will ask the user for the confirmation. Upon user confirmation, it will delete the question. 14. Users can also create the language variants of a particular question by clicking on that particular question title and then clicking on the language button in the Question Detail section. On clicking on the language button the user will get a language selection popup where they have to select the language in which they want their translation. 15. After the selection of language a popup will appear where on the left-hand side the English variant of the question will be visible and on the right-hand side, the selected language variant will be visible. Note: If the question in the selected language variant is already created then it will open in edit mode otherwise it will open in create mode. After filling in all the details, the user can click on the save language button to save all the changes. Users can click on the close button in the top right-hand side of the popup to close the language popup.

This document provides a complete guide for enabling and using Git integration within the Procify platform. It explains how to configure GitHub or Bitbucket repositories, set up SSH access, connect them to your Procify flavor, and work with Git-based version control during development. It covers the end-to-end process—including repository setup, user access, configuring Git details in the Workspace Hub, checking out flavors, and using Git-linked workflows within the Procify environment.
Basics of version control
Go to GitHub. Click “New repository” → create it under your organization account (not personal). Example organization: procify-vsix-integration(only one time setup required by respective app manager)

documents.t: Go to your organization → People / Members section. Click Invite member → invite procify_github. Add procify_user to this organisation https://github.com/orgs/organization_name/people ![Screenshot](./img/git-integration-image1.png) Give read-only access to the repository (permission = Read). documents.t: Note: by default it will checkout from branch which is configured, but there might be case that you don’t have valid access of that branch, so before doing any change checkout that branch. For gitconfigured flavors any change made will not show in existing button(commit All) so you can’t save your changes to public via that button, for committing your change to public commit to corresponding git branch ⚠️ Note — newly created files: The above applies to changes to existing files. When you create a new file (controller / entity / query / rules / view), the Private Node save still records it in the app so it appears in your file explorer — but Build & Deploy reads these file types only from your Git repository, never from the app database. You must commit and push the new file to Git — even if it still holds just the initial template it was scaffolded with — before running Build & Deploy. Skipping this step causes the build to succeed with no warning, but the file will be missing from the deployed app, and the screen using it will fail to load at runtime.

documents.t: A: The file was created but never committed/pushed to the configured Git repository. Build & Deploy sources these file types exclusively from Git, so a file that exists only in the app is not present in the build output. Commit and push the file (even with just its initial template) to the configured branch, then re-run Build & Deploy. If the file is no longer needed, delete it from within Klobase so the stale entry is cleaned up — otherwise the same error recurs on every build.

Dialogs opened via the KloController.openDialog API should be closed using the KloController.closeDialog API, not the sap.m.Dialog's close method. The sap.m.Dialog's close method should only be used when the dialog was opened via the sap.m.Dialog.open() method.

It has been noted that some applications are using the sap.m.Dialog's close method to close dialogs that were opened via the KloController.openDialog API. This can result in inconsistencies and potential issues. To maintain uniformity and prevent problems, it is essential that the KloController.closeDialog API is used to close dialogs opened by the KloController.openDialog API. This document provides guidance on how to correct this issue and ensure that your code follows the correct API usage patterns.

After correcting the code, please perform the following tests to ensure the dialog functions as expected: Open a dialog using KloController.openDialog. Close the dialog using KloController.closeDialog. Ensure that no errors or unexpected behaviors occur.

The Procify Landing Page Settings provides a robust, secure, and performant solution for creating dynamic homepage experiences. By following this documentation and implementing the recommended best practices, developers can create powerful, user-friendly homepage systems that scale with organizational needs while maintaining security and performance standards. For additional support or advanced configuration requirements, consult the Procify development team or refer to the latest API documentation. Note: KloGuid and KloLink controls will be disabled when added inside the embedded subscreens. Since the homepage uses embedded sections to display the screens, they will appear to be disabled as well. If required please use sap.m.Link control.

Need Landing Page Settings to be assigned as TESTER NOTE: For existing applications, a migration script is given to fill the title of the homepage with the title of the screen to show in the tab. It is recommended to do the flavor build once so that the title will reflect in the UI.

SN Steps 1 Assign the homepage_editor as a TESTER to yourself Go to Procify Workspace Hub and assign the latest version of homepage_editor flavor to yourself as a tester. 2 Go to the Landing Page Settings Once assigned, you will get the Upgrade Banner. Once you get the upgrade banner and registration is complete, Click the Hamburger menu and select App Builder Menu Header. Select Landing Page Settings from the Menu. You will be Navigated to the Landing Page Settings. The Menu Editor table includes a search field above the menu tree to help locate a specific Menu ID or Menu Text quickly. How search works: The search matches against both Menu ID and Menu Text, and applies partial/fuzzy matching — you don't need to type the exact full value. If your search term matches a parent menu item only, the filtered tree shows just that parent row (its children are not pulled into the result unless they also match). If your search term matches a child menu item, the filtered tree shows that child along with its parent, so you always retain context of where the item sits in the hierarchy. Note on the child-count indicator: The number shown next to a parent menu item always reflects the total number of children that parent actually has in the full menu tree — not just the ones currently visible in your search results. This count does not change based on your search filter. For example, searching for a parent's name may show a count of 3 even though none of those 3 children match your search text and are therefore not shown below it. Tip: To view all children of a parent, clear the search field (or expand the node directly) rather than relying on the search result or the count next to it.

Middleware (Message Monitoring) is an application that is used for fetching all the information about the entries that are present in the device Info or tenant Info. We can also reprocess the failed messages present inside the error_q of the tenant. Device Info: When we are sending any data/action from server to device we store the message in the device info to know its information and state. In device info, every message is an outgoing message. So, the successfully sent messages are shown here. So, It goes from In queue to success. Tenant Info: When we are sending/fetching any data/action from server to SAP LOCAL or sending data from device to server. We store the message in tenant info to know its information and state. All the messages from Device to Server and SAP Local to server are visible in Inbound MessagesServer Queue Monitor screen. All the messages from Server to SAP Local will be visible to the Outbound queue screen and all the messages from server to device or SAP Local to device will be visible in Device OutboundDevice Queue Monitor screen. Purpose of Message Monitoring​ Message Monitoring is used to show information about messages (UPGRADE, DEBOARD) and the state of the message whether it's in the in-queue, Success, or failed. Every message has a state out of the three states mentioned below : In-Queue: The message is ready for processing. Success: The message has been processed successfully. Failed: Message processing has failed. We can also reprocess the Failed message. The reprocess function is only available for tenant_q. When we are sending/fetching any data/Action from server to device or server to SAP local, we store it in terms of messages to know its information and its state. Navigate to Message Monitoring​ Step 1: Go to the Operations MonitorSystem Monitor option Go to the menu options and select Operations MonitorSys Monitor. Step 2: Click on the required option Click on either Inbound MessagesServer Queue Monitor (Tenant Info**)** or Device OutboundDevice Queue Monitor (Device Info**)** according to your requirements. What type of data will be stored in message monitoring tables:​ It will store the messages for all the transactional data changes. NOTE: Metadata changes will not be reflected in the message monitoring screens.

When we are sending any data/action from server to device, we store the message in the device info to know its information and state. In device info, every message is sent or is in the process of being successfully sent. So, every message is outgoing and never fails. Hence, It goes from in-queue to success. 1.1.1. After processing, either the entries will move to device_log_q (success) or device_error_q (failed). Failed This section shows all entries that failed while processing. An Upsert operation refers to the combination of update and insert actions, where data is either updated if it exists or inserted if it doesn't. When syncing messages, an Upsert scenario behavior typically involves checking if a message already exists in the destination system or database. If it exists, the system will update it; if it doesn't, the system will insert it as a new record. 1.5.1.Upsert Behavior in Middleware for Syncing Messages:​ Data Creation and Update: If the data is new (does not exist in the system), a new entry will be created. If the data already exists, the existing record will be updated instead of creating a new one. Upsert for Root Business Objects (BOs) and Primary Relations: Upsert is only applicable for Root Business Objects (BOs) and their primary relations. For non-primary relations, the Upsert operation will work only if the relation is established using primary keys. Parent-Child Relationship: If a parent is new, but the child data related to the parent already exists, this is considered an unexpected scenario. The user must handle this manually, as it is not automatically managed by the middleware. 1.5.2.Delete Scenario Behavior:​ Parent Entity Deletion: If the parent entity is deleted, the child entities will only be deleted if the user explicitly sends the isdeleted flag as true in the request body for both the parent and child entities. This applies to both primary and aggregate relationships. Child Entity Deletion: If the child entity is deleted, only the child will be deleted. The parent entity will remain intact.

The message forwarding feature helps in generating out-bound messages for devices and external systems for multiple applications when data change is processed in one application. 2.1. In order to maintain mapping flavors needs to be assigned as Manager. Note : In Dev Systems Target flavor version needs to be maintained which is not required in QA/PRD. 2.1. Note : Icon color - green means all the forwarded messages are success Icon color \- red means all the forwarded messages got failed Icon color \- yellow means few got failed and few got success. ![Screenshot](./img/message-monitoring-image16.png) Click on Icon to see the detailed forwarding . Click on Ref Msg Id button to see the forwarded messages. On click on Message ID detailed information can be visible in the new tab. 2.3. Messages that are failed to process can be found in the error q. The error can be found in the error message. Possible reasons a message can fail are. Application logic - When an application logically rejects a request for processing the message. I.e. Adding items to a closed order. Adding shipments to a closed Delivery etc. Suggested solution : Find the root cause why these messages are generated. Eg. screen still allows adding items even if the status of order is closed. And fix the issue / add validation in the client side also. Application bugs - Some cases where application code has a bug, due to which an exception can be raised the message will fail. Eg. Improper null handling, wrong API parameters, typo etc. Transaction User not configured - File processing, transaction user has to be configured with required application & permissions. As all the messages are processed based on the access of the user, messages generated by files need a user to validate against. Refer to the Landscape Editor for how to configure the transaction user. Configured user doesn’t have application assigned : When messages from SAP / File processing are failing with “Access denied: user lacks permission to the required application.” error, it means, the user (SAP communication user / File processing user) does not have that flavor assigned to them. Database Deadlock / Lock Timeout Errors: - When the middleware encounters a transient database deadlock or lock wait timeout (e.g., "Deadlock found when trying to get lock; try restarting transaction"), messages are automatically retried up to 3 times with a 1-second delay (default values) between attempts. - If all retries are exhausted, the message will move to the error queue. - It will have an error message like - "Message <msg_id> failed after 3 retry attempts due to Lock wait timeout exceeded" or "Message <msg_id> failed after 3 retry attempts due to Deadlock found". - The retry settings are configurable via config.json: "MiddlewareRetrySettings": { "DeadlockRetryCount": 3, "RetryDelaySeconds": 1 }

When an application team logs in from multiple or random devices without properly deboarding the previous devices, those devices can continue to be considered active endpoints. As a result, messages may continue to be generated for these endpoints even though the application team is no longer actively using them. Platform Reference: Account Console 7.0 - User Guide — "Whenever any new user registers in the application, a new endpoint ID is created against that account... when they log in again the status becomes Active." Each login is a distinct endpoint; none are deregistered automatically on crash or app closure.
documents.s: 2.1. Multiple Logins Can Create Active Endpoints

documents.t: Because these endpoints remain active, messages generated for them may not be synchronized with the device immediately. Over time, a large number of messages can accumulate in the queue. This can give the impression that a large number of messages are stuck. Platform Reference: Message Monitoring 7.0 - User Guide — In-Queue is defined as "all the data that are currently present in the device_q and which are not processed yet." A high In-Queue count reflects endpoints awaiting sync, not failed or lost messages.
documents.s: 2.2 Messages Can Accumulate in the Queue

documents.t: When the corresponding device comes online , the queued messages are synchronized with the device. Once the server successfully sends the messages and receives the required acknowledgment from the client, the messages move to Success. If the device is offline, the messages remain in the queue until the device becomes available. Platform Reference: Message Monitoring 7.0 - User Guide — device_q entries move to device_log_q (Success) or device_error_q (Failed) only after processing; until then they remain In-Queue, consistent with holding messages for an offline device until it reconnects.
documents.s: 2.3. Messages Are Synchronized When the Device Becomes online

documents.t: A message can reach the device successfully, but the actual processing on the device may still fail. From the server's perspective, the message can be marked as Success when the client acknowledges that the message was received while the device was online. Therefore, Success on the server does not necessarily mean that the message was successfully processed by the application on the device. Platform Reference: Message Monitoring 7.0 - User Guide — "In device info, every message is sent or is in the process of being successfully sent. So, every message is outgoing and never fails. Hence, It goes from in-queue to success." This confirms Success tracks the send/acknowledgment, not on-device application processing.

The application team may not be aware that previously used devices are still registered as active endpoints. This can result in messages continuing to be generated and queued for those endpoints. Note: This is a training/visibility gap rather than a platform defect. Recommend making Sections 1–4 of this topic available to application teams so "stuck message" reports can be self-diagnosed before being escalated as incidents.

A scheduler runs every Sunday to clean up old endpoints. Note: The scheduler currently deboards endpoints that have been inactive for more than 7 days. Once an endpoint is deboarded, its corresponding entry is removed from the endpoint table. Property Value Class name deboardInactiveUsers CRON expression 0 0 0 ? * SUN * (every Sunday at midnight) Current inactivity threshold (this environment) 7 days Platform default threshold 15 days — this environment has been configured below the default Channel type BOTH, unless restricted to DEVICE or BROWSER Table cleaned up Endpoint's entries removed from madm_ep_apps Platform Reference: Account Console 7.0 - User Guide — "Deboard Inactive Users": CRON Job Expression 0 0 0 ? * SUN *, class deboardInactiveUsers, parameters No_of_inactive_days {default: 15} and Channel_type {default: BOTH}; "this scheduler will deboard all the users who are inactive since given days and it will delete the entry of all deboarded endpoints from madm_ep_apps."

If the default 7-day cleanup period does not meet the application's requirements, the scheduler can be customized to use a different endpoint deboarding period. To change it: Go to the job-instances page in Cockpit and locate the deboardInactiveUsers job. Open the job instance's parameters. Update No_of_inactive_days to the desired threshold. Update Channel_type if the cleanup should be restricted to a specific channel. Save. The new threshold takes effect on the job's next scheduled run (the following Sunday, per the fixed CRON expression). Note: The CRON schedule itself (currently fixed to Sunday) is a separate setting from the inactivity threshold — changing how often the job runs, as opposed to how many inactive days it waits, would need to be confirmed as in-scope for this customization request.

Date of Issue: DD MMM YYYY Target Audience: Application Developers, Consultants, Trainees Prepared by: Name Platform Version: XX A User Manual for application creation, knowledge and work reference. Overview The Middleware Message Forwarding feature allows you to automatically sync data changes between different flavors of your application. When data is changed in one flavor (source), it can automatically trigger message generation for users of another flavor (target), ensuring all users stay synchronized regardless of which flavor they're using.

Multi-Flavor Setup​ ✅ You must have multiple flavors (source and target flavors) ✅ Both source and target flavors must be deployed and accessible ✅ Flavors should share common entities that require message sync Entity Design​ ✅ Target Entity: Must exist with identical entity name and table name ✅ Target Entity: Must have ENDPOINT_RESOLVER event configured with proper implementation

Administrative Access​ ✅ Access to Operations Monitor application for configuration ✅ Permissions to create/modify Middleware Message Routing entries ✅ Message monitoring access for troubleshooting and monitoring Development Environment​ ✅ Private node setup with DEV landscape (for testing) ✅ Access to both source and target flavor codebases ✅ Debugging capabilities in development environment

Message Processing Infrastructure​ ✅ Message processing must be functional Monitoring Tools​ ✅ Message Monitoring screen access for tracking forwarded messages ✅ Queue Monitor for viewing message queues and error queues ✅ Log access for troubleshooting and debugging

Development Team​ ✅ Understanding of entity event implementation (ENDPOINT_RESOLVER) ✅ Familiarity with addEndpoint() method usage ✅ Knowledge of message queue and processing ✅ Experience with multi-flavor application development Configuration Team​ ✅ Understanding of flavor versioning and deployment ✅ Knowledge of landscape management (DEV/TEST/PROD) ✅ Familiarity with Operations Monitor configuration tools

To enable message forwarding, you need to configure mappings in the Mw Message Routing Screen in Operations Monitor: Configuration Screen - Mw Message Routing Access this screen through Operations Monitor > Middleware Message Routing Required Fields​ Source Flavor: The flavor where changes originate Target Flavor: The flavor that where the changes should be also be forwarded for message generation. Is Active: Set to true to enable forwarding Target Version: Only for DEV Specify a particular version of the target flavor. Use this for debugging purposes. In QA & Production, the latest version is used. Configuration Steps​ Open Operations Monitor application Navigate to "Middleware Message Routing" Click "Add New" to create a mapping Fill in Source Flavor and Target Flavor names Set "Is Active" to true Save the configuration

documents.t: Multi-Flavor Applications​ If your application has multiple flavors (e.g., online and offline versions) that share common entities, this feature ensures data consistency across all flavors. Example Scenarios:​ Portal + Mobile App: Changes made in the web portal should sync to mobile app users Hierarchical Applications: Parent flavor changes should sync to child flavor users How Does It Work ?​ Data Change Trigger: When you create, update, or delete data in a source flavor Automatic Detection: The system detects if forwarding is configured for that flavor in Middleware Message Routing ( Operations Monitor ) Trigger Endpoint Resolver: The ENDPOINT_RESOLVER event will be triggered in target flavor if the same entity exists. Message Generation: Messages are generated for target flavor users based on the target flavor ENDPOINT_RESOLVER logic. Synchronized Delivery: All related messages share the same reference ID for tracking

documents.t: Target Entity Setup​ Your target entity must have:​ Same entity name as source entity Same table name (tb field) as source entity ENDPOINT_RESOLVER event configured Event implementation in the entity class file Example Entity Event Implementation​ // In your entity class file (e.g., src/flavor/entity/your_entity.ts) async onEndpointResolver(txn, dataObj, headers) { // Your logic to determine which users/endpoints should receive messages this.addEndpoint(userList, EndpointType.User, ChannelType.Both); }

documents.t: When message forwarding fails, check the Error Queue for detailed information: Error queue entry showing failed forwarding message with MSG_FORWARD type Error Queue Analysis​ Message Type: Look for "MSG_FORWARD" type entries Error Details: Review error messages for troubleshooting Retry Options: Use message reprocessing to retry failed forwards

documents.t: Message Generation​ Additional Messages: You'll see target flavor messages in device/tenant queues Message Grouping: Related messages share the same reference ID Cross-Flavor Sync: Changes in source flavor should trigger messages in target flavor Error Handling​ Isolated Failures: If target flavor processing fails, source transaction still completes Error Queue Entries: Failed forwards create entries in error queue with type MSG_FORWARD Retry Capability: Failed messages forwarding can be reprocessed later. It will only retry the forwarding, not the original transaction. The dirty state and from state is preserved from the original transaction.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Middleware Message Forwarding - 4. How to use the feature

documents.t: What is a Reference ID?​ The reference ID (ref_msg_id) is a unique identifier that groups all messages generated from a single transaction. How It Works​ Original Message → ref_msg_id: "ABC123" ├── Source Flavor Message → ref_msg_id: "ABC123" ├── Target Flavor 1 Message → ref_msg_id: "ABC123" └── Target Flavor 2 Message → ref_msg_id: "ABC123"

documents.t: In your entity event handlers, you can detect if the event was triggered by message forwarding: async onEndpointResolver() { let headers = await this.getHeaders(); let sourceApp = headers.src_app; let currentFlavor = this.txn.$SYSTEM.flavor; if (sourceApp !== currentFlavor) { // This event was triggered by message forwarding this.info(`Message forwarded from ${sourceApp} to ${currentFlavor}`); } else { // This is a normal event execution } }

documents.t: Configuration Management​ Minimal Mappings: Only configure necessary flavor mappings Environment-Specific: Use similar configurations for DEV/TEST/PROD Regular Review: Periodically audit your forwarding configurations Testing Strategy​ Verify End-to-End: Test complete data flow from source to target users Monitor Queues: Watch queue growth during testing Check Error Logs: Review error queues for any issues

documents.t: The Callbacks tab is available within a notification template in the Notification Editor. It allows you to register server-side callback methods that run when the notification is being processed, enabling you to attach files dynamically to outgoing emails. Each callback method is defined by a name and a sequence number that controls the order in which it is executed. Callbacks tab inside a notification template in Notification Editor What you can do in the Callbacks Tab View all registered callback methods for the template, listed in the execution sequence. Add a new callback by entering a method name. This name must match the method implemented in the notification callback file. Delete an existing callback by selecting it and clicking Delete. Reorder callbacks by dragging and dropping rows in edit mode. The sequence number determines the order in which methods run and the order attachments are added to the email. Click the More Info button to see the list of allowed attachment file types. Only files with allowed extensions will be attached to the email — others are silently skipped. Key Rules The method name entered here must exactly match the method name written in the notification callback file, which extends KloNotification. Sequence numbers control both execution order and attachment order in the final email. Reordering is only possible in edit mode. Drag handles appear on each row when edit mode is active. Callbacks with disallowed file types are skipped gracefully without failing the notification. For implementation details, code examples, and how to write the callback file, refer to the Notification Developer Guide.
Working with Template Variables and Rich Text Formatting
documents.s: Notification Modeler — Email Template User Guide

documents.t: When creating email templates, you can use template variables to insert dynamic content. Template variables look like this: <%= variable_name %> Common Examples: <%= rfx_no %> - Shows the RFx number <%= rfx_description %> - Shows the RFx title <%= new Date(rfx_closing_date).toLocaleString() %> - Shows the closing date <%= supplier_name %> - Shows the supplier name

DO NOT apply text formatting (bold, italic, underline, etc.) to template variables themselves. The rich text editor inserts invisible HTML tags when you format text. These tags break the template variables and cause errors.
documents.s: Important Rule: Formatting and Template Variables

documents.t: Example 1: Bold label, normal variable Steps: Type your text: Closing Date: <%= new Date(rfx_closing_date).toLocaleString() %> Select only "Closing Date:" (not the <%= %> part) Click the Bold button Result: Closing Date: <%= new Date(rfx_closing_date).toLocaleString() %> Example 2: Variable within formatted sentence Steps: Type: The RFx <%= rfx_no %> has been closed. Select "The RFx" (before the variable) and click Bold Select "has been closed" (after the variable) and click Bold separately Leave the <%= rfx_no %> part unformatted

Wrong Right Select entire line with <%= %> and click Bold Select only the text labels, not <%= %> Type <%= rfx_no %> then format it Type it, leave it unformatted Copy-paste formatted text containing <%= %> Paste as plain text, then format around <%= %> Use bullet points that include <%= %> Put <%= %> on separate line or outside bullets

Step 1: Switch to HTML View If available, switch to HTML view to see your template variables clearly. Step 2: Type your content with variables RFx Title: <%= rfx_description %> Closing Date: <%= new Date(rfx_closing_date).toLocaleString() %> Step 3: Format carefully Highlight only "RFx Title:" (exclude the <%= %> part) Click Bold button Repeat for "Closing Date:" Step 4: Verify in HTML view RFx Title: <%= rfx_description %> Closing Date: <%= new Date(rfx_closing_date).toLocaleString() %> Step 5: Test before saving Use "Preview" button if available Check for error messages

Error Message: "Unexpected token '<' while compiling ejs" Cause: You accidentally formatted a template variable. Solution: Switch to HTML view Find the template variable mentioned in the error Look for HTML tags like <strong>, <em>, <span> inside <%= %> Remove the HTML tags from inside the template variable Reapply formatting only to the text outside <%= %>

Task How To Make a label bold Select label text only (not <%= %>), click Bold Add new variable Type <%= variable_name %>, leave unformatted Format around variable Format text before and after separately Fix error Switch to HTML view, remove tags from inside <%= %> Verify template Check HTML view: no tags between <%= and %>

If you see template errors: Switch to HTML View Check that no <strong>, <b>, <em>, <i>, <span> tags are inside <%= %> Use HTML view for templates - It's easier to see what's happening Format first, add variables later - Format your static text, then insert <%= %> variables in unformatted areas Keep variables simple - Don't try to format dynamic content; format the labels instead Test with sample data - Always test your template
Notification Modeler Guide Date of Issue: September 2023 Training Version Number: 7.0 Target Audience: Developers, Clients.

A notification is a message, email, icon, or another symbol that appears when an application wants you to pay attention. Notifications are a way to alert you on the various important facts that have happened in your application that are worth your attention while you are not using the application. Notification Modeler is used to create a notification. One can create, edit, copy, and delete the different types of notifications in this editor. This tool is used to perform CRUD operations for the Notifications.
documents.s: Notification Modeler — Introduction To Notification Modeler

documents.t: In the Editor, upon selecting any particular App, it will show the list of notifications that are listed for that app. For a template sample click here. Upon clicking on the notification template ID, a detailed screen will open where we can check the notification details. In this detail section, users can perform CRUD operations on notifications.

The elements on the Notification Modeler screen have been explained below: Elements Description Template ID A Unique ID for each Notification. Description This is the description or implication for the Notifications. Module Type Notifications are used in two places, BOL and Workflow. To differentiate these two categories Module type has been introduced. Entity An entity is a data object created to store information about the entity in a table format. An entity can be created in the BOL Editor. Entity Object Type Object type is a unique identifier that helps understand the entities' possible behaviour. Channel It denotes the types of Notifications (e.g.: Email, App, SMS) FO Owning app.

documents.t: To add an action for the page, add an aggregation “kloAction” for the page. Once the kloAction is added, create a new button control for the action. After adding a control add properties for that button control.

Similar to page actions we can add actions to our sections. To add actions for our sections kloToolbar needs to be added for that section. After adding kloToolbar add an aggregation kloAction for the kloToolbar. After adding kloAction aggregation follow the same steps as page actions. On click of add button:
An aggregation is a way for one control (called a parent) to reference another subordinate control (called a child).

For Grid, Tree, and Auto Grid section types, the Builder automatically applies horizontal alignment (hAlign) and text align property based on the control type and its associated binding. So the column header and the control will be aligned as per the standards based on the domain and control type Numeric Field Alignment​ If a control is bound to a property whose domain type is Integer or Decimal, the Builder automatically adds the hAlign config property and textAlign control property with the value Right. This automatic alignment is applied only when: The control is an input-based control. The control is bound to a property of domain type Integer or Decimal. Alignment Updates on Control Changes​ During updates, if: A control's value property or dsrc is modified, or A new binding is added to the control, the Builder automatically detects the bound property and updates the alignment accordingly. Domain/data type Data alignment Header Alignment Boolean [if control is checkbox or switch] Center Center Blob N/A N/A String Left Left Clob Left Left Date Left Left Decimal Right Right Integer(16) Right Right Integer(32) Right Right Integer(64) Right Right Integer(8) Right Right Timestamp Left Left Control-Specific Alignment Rules​ The following alignment rules are applied automatically: Control Type hAlign Value Switch, Check Box Center Button, KloAction Right Auto Grid Behavior​ For Auto Grid sections, automatic alignment is applied only in the Desktop view. For the Mobile view, the default alignment behavior is retained and no automatic alignment adjustments are applied.

documents.t: onPageInit​ onPageInit hook method will be called only once as soon as the controller is loaded The transaction, model , and the UI is yet to be created for this, so those will not be available in this method. onPageModelReady​ onPageModelReady event will be called when the model is created and the transnodes are initialized, but the data is not set to the model yet. From this hook method developer can call skipModelPreparation method which will skip setting the data and executing the query. If the developer skips the model preparation, then developer should be responsible for setting the data is the model onPageEnter​ onPageEnter hook method will be called whenever the page enters the visible area by means of navigation(both forward and backward navigation). If the navigation is within the same page, this method will not be triggered onPageExit**:**​ onPageExit hook method will be called in the source page whenever the user navigates to a different page onPageDestroy: onPageDestroy hook method will be called only once when the page is destroyed. Page will be destroyed during the back navigation Example : if you are navigating back from PageB to pageA then PageB will be destroyed

Controls are used to define the appearance and behaviour parts of the section. Types of controls: Open UI5 controls Klo controls
5.7 kloControls contains all the information about the kloTouch controls.
The class field in the property section of the control describes the class of the control.

A tooltip is often used to specify extra information about the elements when the user moves the mouse pointer over an element. Follow the following steps to use the tooltip for the screen title: Step 1: Add two properties to the screen. Step 2: Mark isTitleTooltipRequired as ‘true’ and provide value(as string) to titleTooltip. Now when you hover on the title of the screen you will show the titleTooltip value. Refer to this for more information Tooltip for Screen Title
The label field in the control’s property section is to set whether the label is needed for the control or not (specific for card and form type section).

The card layout provides you with only one column. Hence, earlier there was no option to provide a label. But, since we are adding multiple controls in the same column, it is better to identify the control with the label. Now, with the provided property, it is possible to put labels on the controls inside the card layout. Step 1: Add the property islabelForCardRequired to the property subscreen and mark it as ‘true’. Note: If you have already added the label during the entity creation for that property, then that label will appear after adding the islabelForCardRequired as true. And if you haven’t added the label during the entity creation or you want to add another label then you can simply provide your text in the ‘label’ property.

In the tree section, we can drag and drop the controls from one section to another. OR Create a new control. Right-click on the section where the control needs to be added, click on ‘New’ and then click on ‘Controls’ to add a control for that section. After clicking on ‘Controls’ below page will appear to add the control. Note: Control id should be unique under a section (Two controls / config /section toolbar can’t have same id) Adding control without binding i.e. if dsrc or value field is empty, it will show a warning message.
Klotouch Editor is divided into four major sections, which are listed below. Tree Preview Detail Page Data Model

The tree section in the kloTouch editor contains the hierarchy of the page. The tree will contain no data unless a page is created/selected from the toolbar. Once a page is created/selected it shall automatically reflect in the tree section.
Expand All option is to expand all the collapsed sections (sections, pageLayout, controls, pageArea, actions).
Collapse All option is to collapse all the expanded sections (sections, pageLayout, wcontrols, pageArea, actions).

This filter button will open a popup as : It will contain fuzzy search, section drop-down and clear filter option. The use of fuzzy search is to filter the items based on the Ids. Section dropdown is used to select and preview a particular section / pageArea of the page. This will filter the tree only for the selected section and its children. Clear filters are used to clear the filters applied.
Using the cut copy-paste options, we are able to copy paste the controls/section /pageAreas. Note: These buttons are inactive in read-only mode.

The create section button is used to create a section and to add required properties from a particular type of transnode. Clicking on this button, it will open a popup : In the above popup, we need to mention section id, section title, section type and page data model with which the section is supposed to be binded. After selecting the page data model, properties list will come in the Page Data Model Node section from where we can select the required properties. Note: We can edit the section after creation from the Editor.
The Preview section is to preview the page before the final execution.

This is also known as the Preview type. The use of preview types is to see the look and feel of the same page on different types of devices. The devices that it can be viewed on are given below. Any new version of the device comes, likewise, it will be updated. Preview samples

Usage of the auto-refresh button is to refresh the preview in design time i.e. if the auto-refresh is enabled whenever the user changes anything in the page’s metadata it will be previewed (auto-refreshed) automatically.
The usage of the preview or refresh button is to refresh the preview page to make the changes visible.
The full preview option is used to view the page in full view.
The close option is to hide the preview section, to enable the preview section make use of the section toggle buttons Buttons Identity To Expand to Full Screen. To Close the Preview Section.

DnD on Preview is a drag-and-drop feature. It is an option to Drag and Drop properties and elements in multiple ways. DnD from Unused to MainTree: Step 1: From the page data model, select the transnode, go to its unused property tab and drag the Property. Step 2: Drop that Property to any section you want. After preview, the newly added property will be shown on the screen. DnD from MainTree to MainTree: Users can Drag and Drop any main tree element across the tree. Step 1: Drag an element from any section and Drop it into the different sections in the same tree. When an element is dragged and dropped between sections, a prompt appears asking whether to Move or Copy the element. Selecting Move removes the element from the source section and places it in the target section, while selecting Copy duplicates the element in the target section without affecting the source. Note: The Move and Copy options are shown only when the drag-and-drop action occurs between two different sections.
Details of the item selected in the tree section will be shown in this detail section: This depicts the name or ID of the item selected in the tree.

The property tab in the detail section displays the properties that are added and options to add new properties that are associated with the selected item (page, pageArea, pageLayout, sections, controls). Refer to this to understand binding concepts. Value:​ The value field will hold the value provided for the property. Path:​ In this path field, users can only bind with exactly one property or value. This can be used if there is only one property to bind. Parts:​ In this path field, users can bind multiple properties or values. This can be used if multiple values or properties need to be provided for binding. (Note: If we are using formatter function, then it is mandatory to provide either parts or path value) Formatter Functions​ Controller function name (formatter function) can be given for the field. Type:​ In the type field, the user can provide the datatype for the control’s value. Formatter Options:​ Formatter options define how a value is formatted and displayed in the UI. Validation Constraint:​ Constraints are optional and define how an input value that is entered in the UI should look like. During parsing, the value is validated against these constraints. For example, an Integer type has a constraint for the maximum that is automatically validated when parsing the input values. Add new Property:​ To add a new property, click on the add icon in the property section toolbar. On click of the add icon the properties associated with the control will be listed. Click on the property that needs to be added, it will be added to the control. Provide the property value for the newly added property. Property Group:​ The Property group consists of the following: Property Group Details Appearance The appearance property group will filter the properties that are responsible for the appearance of the control. Example: visible, textAlign, wrapping, textDirection. Data The data property group will filter the properties that are responsible for the binding values of the control. Example: value, src, text, href. Dimension Dimension property group will filter the properties that are responsible for the dimensions of the control. Example: width, size, height. Behaviour The behaviour property group will filter the properties that are responsible for the behaviour of a control. Example: editable, enabled. Misc Properties other than the above-mentioned groups will come under Misc. Select All/ None:​ This option is used to select/unselect all the properties. Cut:​ This option is to cut and paste the property of one control to another control. Copy and Paste:​ The Copy and Paste options are used to copy/paste one or more properties from one control to another. Delete Property:​ To delete a property, select the property that needs to be deleted and click on the delete icon in the properties section toolbar.

The Aggregations tab in the detail section displays the aggregations that are associated with the selected item (page, pageArea, sections, controls) Path:​ Binding Path addresses the different properties and lists in a model and defines how a node in the hierarchical data tree can be found. Examples: $M>/list, $M>/items Add new Aggregation:​ To add a new aggregation click on the add icon in the aggregation section toolbar. On click of the add icon the aggregations associated with the control will be listed. Click on the aggregation that needs to be added, it will be added to the control. Select All/ None​ This option is being used to select/unselect all the aggregations. Cut​ This option is to cut and paste the aggregations of one control into another control. Copy and Paste​ The Copy and paste options are being used to copy/paste one or more aggregations from one control to another. Delete Aggregation:​ For delete, select the aggregation that you want to delete. And click on the delete icon in the aggregation toolbar.

The Events tab in the detail section displays the events that are associated with the selected item (page, pageArea, sections, controls). Functions​ The controller function name should be given in the field, which will be called in case of the event. Example of Controller function: Parameters​ The values passed in the field can be accessible in the function as a parameter. Add new Event:​ To add a new event click on the add icon in the event section toolbar. On click of the add icon the events associated with the control will be listed. Click on the event that needs to be added, it will be added to the control/sections / pageArea. Note: If we are adding a new event then, it is necessary to add or select the function name. If we are adding a function from the vh as OpenDialog, it will show a popup with all the pageAreas to select,from which we want to navigate. Select All/ None:​ This option is being used to select/unselect all the events. Cut:​ This option is to cut and paste the event of one control to another control. Copy and Paste:​ Copy and paste options are being used to copy/paste one or more events from one control to another. Delete Event:​ To delete an event select the event and click on the delete button from the toolbar. Events list on page In the page-level events, we have an option to see the list of events added to this page. Step 1: Select the page in the Page Builder page tree section Step 2: Select the events tab in the page detail section Step 3: enable the toggle button Once it is enabled, all the events added to this page will be listed below

NavTo is a kloController API that is used for navigation across the application. In the Events tab of the Page Builder, if we select NavTo as an event method, the below parameters will reflect for NavTo. Parameters for Navigation​ The following are the parameters for the navigation: Target Page: It is an F4 of the screens where sections of the current screen, related screen (screens created with related entities) and all the screens of the respected app are present. Section: It is an F4 of all the pagelayouts, pageAreas and sections of the target page. Tags: It shows all the TagIDs maintained in the target screen. Mode: It is a dropdown for different screen modes. App Data: It is a field where the application can send any data while navigating to the target screen. Page Data Model: It is a F4 of all the Data models of the target page. Active Index: It accepts the index to which setActive will be called in the list. Page Data Model Map: It is an array of JSON which expect SourceTransNode & TargetTransnode(i.e SourcetransNode data will be copied to TargetTransnode) Query Parameters: It is for navigation by query(navByQuery). Share Mode: This is for setting whether the mode will be shared after navigating between the source and target pages. Share Model: This is for setting whether the transaction will be shared after navigating between the source and target page.

The Style Class tab in the detail section displays the quick styles that are available for the control/pageArea/sections. There are style classes that have already been added and there are options to add a new style class for the selected item (pageArea, sections, controls). QuickAdd:​ Quick Add for Sections:​ Below is the list of quick adds available for specific section types: Section types Quick Adds Card, card List Card styles Grid Grid styles Card Styles:​ Grid Styles:​ Quick Add for Controls:​ Below is the list of quick adds available for specific controls: Controls Quick Add Icon Font size, Text color Text, Label, Title, Link Font size, Text color, Bold, Italic, Underline Button, Switch, info label Font Size, Background color, Text Color, color combination, Bold, Italic, underline, border style Input, TextArea, DatePicker, TimePicker, DateTimePicker, MultiCombobox, MultiInput, SearchField, comboBox Font size, Text color, Bold, Italic, Underline, border style Font Size:​ Text Colour:​ Bold:​ Italic:​ Underline:​ Background color:​ Color Combination:​ Specific Style:​ Category:​ In this category field, we can choose the style category that needs to be applied to the selected item. Style Class:​ Class names should be provided for this field, which will be applied to the selected items. Style class works after selecting the category. In the below image, we have taken the border as our category. Hence, border options are seen in the StyleClass. Note: The style class should not be empty. Format Rule: Always: If the format rule is marked as always, it will always apply the style. Text Contains: If the format rule is marked as the text contains, it will apply the style if the value contains the one mentioned in the format value. Formula: If the format rule is marked as formula, it will apply the expression maintained in the format value field and based on the result set of the expression (result is expected to be true or false) the style class will be applied to that control Example Format value for formula : {= ${$M>/temp/save}?true:false} Format Value:​ If the format rule is marked with text contain, then text will be taken from this format value field and it will be compared with the control’s value. If the format rule is marked with a formula, then the expression will be taken from this format value field and based on the result set(the result should be expected to be true or false) of the expression, the style class will be set. Example Format value for formula : {= ${$M>/temp/save}?true:false} Full Row:​ If the full row is marked as true, then the style class will be applied to the entire row, where the control is placed. Note: For tree screen type, full-row in style class will be applicable only when the section’s screen type is full row, it will not work for control for control type tree tables. Add new Style Class:​ To add a new style class click on the add icon in the style class section toolbar. On clicking the add icon, a new entry will be created for the style class. Select the category and add the style class accordingly. Cut**,** copy, and paste:​ For cut, copy, and paste you need to select the styleclass and then use the cut, copy, and paste accordingly. Delete​ Select the StyleClass item you want to delete and then click on the delete icon from the toolbar. Grid Cell Coloring:​ For adding css(background) to whole cell of grid section, user can do following: Add user defined class in control of grid section use :has Pseudo-class, and do required styling Example: as given below: td:has(.invAmountColorWholeCell) { background: #0c8123; }

Vienable is the short form of visible and enable. The Vienable tab in the detail section displays the vienable dashboard and UI Auth for the page. Toolbar:​ Page Entity:​ Copy and paste:​ Upload and Download Excel:​ Role Info:​ Status Info:​ Vienable toggle button Info:​ 2.3.5(i). Vienable DashBoard:​ Control ID:​ The Control ID column displays the available controls on the page. Entity:​ The transNode of which the control is bound. If it is not marked as true, status and role-based vienable will not work. Permission:​ The permission of the entity in flavor on which control/element visibility will be decided for logged-in users. If permission is not filled by developer, then proceeds with with vienable calculation If permission is filled by developer, but filled permission not given for logged in user, then the current control/element will be hidden by skipping vienable calculation If permission is filled by developer, filled permission given for logged in user, then proceeds with with vienable calculation Show As Label:​ If the control is disabled, and the showAsLabel is marked as true then the disabled control will be rendered as a label. Page Size(S, M, L, XL):​ The page sizes S, M, L, and XL define small, medium, large, and extra-large size page resolutions. If the control is marked as non-visible for page size S, then the control will be hidden for that particular resolution. If the control is marked as disabled for page size S, then the control will be disabled for that particular resolution. Note: The resolution will be considered based on the parent section’s resolution for control. page Mode (Create, Edit, Display, Review):​ There are four modes for a page: Create, Edit, Display, and Review. Among the page modes display will be the default mode. We can change the page modes based on the requirements. Role:​ Role-based vienable helps the control to be visible/enabled based on the current logged-in person’s role and object type of the bound entity. For this role-based configuration, KloTuner is used. For role-based vienable, config has to be maintained for the respective entity. If it is not maintained in the entity level, It will consider the role maintained in the app-level. While configuring the config table, provide the s_role_rollup value as below: Role s_role_up Owner 10 Supervisor 20 Reviewer 30 Overlooker 40 Status Group():​ Status: open, approved, accepted, processed, rejected, completed. Based on the s_status_group, s_status, and object type for that particular entity, we will be able to make the control visible/enabled. For status-based configuration, Klotuner is used. Note: Similar to role-based vienable, status-based vienable status configs have to be maintained for the entity. Result:​ In the result column, we can see the final result of how the controls will be rendered, for the selected page mode, selected role, and selected status group. The yellow background in the column header represents the selection of the column. 2.3.5(ii). UI Auth:​ Element Id:​ It is the control ID of the control. Object Type:​ For this object type, UI Auth will be applied. Role:​ For this role, the UI Auth will be applied. Status:​ For this status, UI Auth will be applied. Mode:​ For this mode, UI Auth will be applied. Mode Value:​ This will determine the control’s visibility / enableness. Add new UI Auth:​ To add a new UI Auth click on the add icon in the toolbar of the UI Auth section. On click of the add icon, a popup will be displayed. In the popup select the control for which UI Auth needs to be applied. Select the role, mode, object type, and status after selecting press OK. A new entry will be added in the UI Auth section. Vienable Runtime precedence:​ If all the vienable sections (screen size, screen mode, role, status) are maintained for control, below will be the flow of the section it will take into consideration.

The Modeller tab in the detail section displays the modeller only if the modeller is available for the selected section type. A modeller is generally used for modelling the sections. To access the modeller of a section select that particular section in the tree section to preview that particular section. Card & cardList Modeller:​ WYSWYG (What You See What You Get) Card WYSWYG allows the users to arrange/resize controls of the Card. The Card WYSWYG is available in the tab called “Modeller” of the kloTouch Editor if the section type is given as cardlist/card. These are the following steps to use WYSWYG: Step 1: Select the section (of type “cardlist” or ”card”) or any child of the section (of type “cardlist” or ”card”). Step 2: Open the “Modeller” tab. Users can arrange/resize controls as required. Step 3: For arranging the controls, the user can simply drag a control and drop it anywhere on the axis as per the requirement. While doing the arrangement or resizing, if any other control exists in the same axis, red lines will be shown. Step 4: For resizing the controls, Users can simply click on the controls and resize them as they want. Before resizing: After resizing: NOTE: Users can select multiple controls(by holding the control) and “Make the same size” (Vertically/Horizontally). Reveal Grid: With this button, one can enable and disable the gridlines. Tabular Card Modeller: On clicking this button, a tabular card modeller will open where the user can manually provide a column/row span for the alignment of the card/cardList. Alignment: Options for Alignment, space distribution, equal size: Modeller Size: To make the card modeller screen size the selected item’s size one uses the modeller size (Tab, Desktop, etc) tab.(This option has been disabled: To use this, change the screen resolution from preview type) Absolute/Relative: The absolute button will make the modeller as the previous version without additional features. The card is generally a css gridlayout and the cardlist is generally a list of css grid layouts. Using this grid modeller we will be able to change the column width, we can assign filters, and sort for a particular column. Pivot Modeller:​ There are two types of pivot modellers Design time Run time Note: The difference between the design time and run time modeller is that the design time modeller cannot be modified by end users it is predefined by the developers. The design time pivot can be set as the default view of the section by use of the ‘default report’ property of the section. Design Time Modeller :​ Design time pivot will be created by the developers which will be predefined, and cannot be modified by the end users. Step 2: Now in the toolbar detail, add two properties (reportSelectionField and pivotModellerButton) and mark these properties as true. Model Path/TransNode:​ Properties Description Entity This field will display the entity name that is associated with the transNode. Property Description Displays the property description. folded_from This field will display from where the path is folded. node_type Node Type determines the type of the model path. on_arrive Refer to onArrive. q_auto_update If this is marked as true, then any change in the transactional data will be automatically updated in the model. q_object_group The Object group mentioned here will be filtered for the particular query type. q_object_type The object type mentioned here will be filtered for the particular query type. q_pin Coming Soon q_saved_qur_action Refer to q_saved_qur_action q_saved_qur_id This implicates the saved query ID which needs to be fired along with the search (if q_saved_qur_action is marked as fill). relation This field displays the name of the transNode. screenid This field displays the page ID. set_active_if Refer to Set_active_if Node Type:​ Entity: Entity defines a single entity (single row in a database table). Entity Set: An entity set is a set of entities (an entire table in a database). Query: Query which is associated with the entity. Other: Other types of transnode represent that the node is not associated with any entity. Its data can be bound from the controller. onArrive:​ Blank: If the model path is marked as blank then the data will not be set to its folded path. First: If the model path is marked as first then the first index of its entityset(folded from) will be set. History: If the model path is marked as history then it records the active index of the entityset. For example: if the model path is marked as history, then each selection of entity will be recorded. None: If the model path is marked as none then the data will not be set for that path. Set_active_if:​ Set active is classified into three categories as listed below: Always: Always defines navigation without any pre-conditions except menu navigation. Saved: Saved means navigation is permitted only if there is no dirty object in the transaction. If dirty entities are found, the Save confirmation dialog comes to ask the user if he/she wants to save the changes, otherwise, navigation is cancelled. Valid: Valid is a default value. Valid means navigation is permitted if there are no dirty objects or dirty objects are in a valid state with no error. If dirty objects are there and in an error state, the errors are highlighted on the page for the user to correct before moving forward. If the mode path’s set_active_if is provided as “valid”, on time of navigation the onValidate function (if the function is maintained in the <entity_name>.ts file) will be called. Please refer to the below matrix for all combinations of set_active_if: always saved valid Within Screen Same index of entityset(tab selection change) CREATE No Validation, No Dirty Popup No Dirty Popup No Validation Not CREATE No Validation, No Dirty Popup Dirty Popup Validation Different index of entityset Any No Validation, No Dirty Popup Dirty Popup Validation Close Detail Any No Validation, No Dirty Popup Dirty Popup Validation Different Screen Through Manu Any Dirty Popup Dirty Popup Dirty Popup Through Link inside screen Any No Validation, No Dirty Popup Dirty Popup Validation q_saved_qur_action:​ Execute: Execute will autofire the query while rendering the page. This is set as the default value. Fill: If the q_saved_qur_action is marked as true then the “q_saved_qur_id” will be filled on search. None: None means it will take no action.

KloTouch module of Framework is providing default Page Data Models: Properties Usage deviceInfo Indicates user’s device type with Boolean values for properties: desktop, tablet, phone Example Binding: {= ${$M>/deviceInfo/desktop} } $M: Model deviceInfo: Page Data Model Desktop: Property perm Contains all enabled permissions in app Example Binding: {= ${$M>/perm/d_sales=CR_ACC} } $M: Model perm: Page Data Model d_sales=CR_ACC: Getter for Create permission enabled in entity d_sames which returns Boolean value env_user Contains all Env User Properties Example Binding: {= ${$M>/env_user/owning_bp} !== 'BP001' ? true : false } $M: Model env_user: Page Data Model role: One of the properties of Env User env_system Contains all System Data(transaction.$SYSTEM) Properties Example Binding: {= ${$M>/env_system/roleID} !== 'DEVELOPER' ? true : false } $M: Model env_system: Page Data Model role: One of the properties of System Data(transaction.$SYSTEM)

By using this embedded section we can embed sections or containers from other pages to our current page. Note: KloGuid and KloLink controls will be disabled when added inside the embedded subscreens. Also, the title, icon and actions provided for the embedded subscreen will not be rendered. Page layout type” flexible_col” is not supported inside embedded section.

To create an embedded page create a page Layout in the page where the section is embedded from. In our current page create an embedded section. In the layout data of the embedded section provide the value below: flavor.pageId.pageContainerId if it's a separate app. pageId.pageContainerId if the embedding page is from the same app. Note: Developers can pass supported navTo() properties from a parent screen to an embedded child screen. TN and NT parameters will be passed to child functions (such as onPageEnter() and onSectionEnter()) only when they are explicitly maintained in the embedded section's screenParameters configuration.

The properties available in the embedded config are listed below. Embedded config can be added from context menu of the embedded section NAME TYPE DEFAULT VALUE DESCRIPTION flavor string - App from which the page should be picked from. App is mandatory only if the app of the screen to be embedded and the app of the hosting page are different. screenid string - ID of the screen. Mandatory subscreenid string - ID of the subscreen. Mandatory. isTransactionShared boolean false If true, the hosting screen and the embedded screen will share the transaction. Else, transaction will be different for both the screens isSharemode boolean false If true, the hosting screen and embedded screen will share the mode. When mode is set via the controller for the hosting screen, the same screen will be set to the embedded screen as well and vice-versa. Else, the mode will not be shared. When set to the hosting screen, the mode will not be set to the embedded screen. tnmap Array<JSON> - An array of JSON with the keys fromtn and totn. The value of the keys should be the transnode relation ID of the host screen and embedded screen respectively. The transnode of the embedded screen will be added as a child to the transnode of the hosting screen so that when setActive is called on the parent transnode, data will be set on child. Example : [{"fromtn": "no_hdr_list", "totn": "detail_embedded"}] screenParameters INavToData This property expects a JSON the same as the navTo parameters. All the navTo parameters can be passed here. Flavor, Screen ID, subscreen ID, isTransactionShared, isSharemode and tnmap can also be passed as key-value pair here instead of separate properties.

Page Builder User Guide- 7.0 Date of Issue: January 2023 Target Audience: Application Developer, Consultants. A User Manual for application creation, knowledge, and work reference.

What is kloTouch? kloBase platform is a modern low-code platform to build enterprise-class cloud-enabled portals and mobile business applications. Its unique layered development empowers to build powerful reusable models for the continuously evolving business needs. kloTouch is a low-code visual designer tool that helps application development efficiently and effectively. What is the objective of kloTouch? kloTouch is a visual designing Page Builder that is effective in building applications that work on portals and mobile applications. kloTouch has the following objectives: Ease of Operating: It involves least to no complex coding, thus, making it an easy-to-use tool, not only for the modellers but also for common people with limited technical knowledge. Efficient: This Page Builder is programmed in a manner that requires a limited to negligible coding process. This prevents the modellers and developers from losing time by writing lengthy codes, thus saving time. Rich In-Built Features: Multiple add-ons and real-time notifications to name a few, help make it a featureful application.

All the page Area ID(s) provided in the page’s layout section will implement the master-detail-detail paradigm by displaying up to three pages (page Areas) in separate columns. For a Flexible column layout, only three columns will be rendered, if more than three layout containers are provided in the layout section it will take the first three layout containers/sections. Configuration:​ For using the flexible column layout, select the screenType of a pageLayout as flexi_column. In the layout section of that pageLayout add the layouts. The setLayout() method was used in Flexible Column to define the layout width. As Flexible Column is now deprecated, it is recommended to use setFirstColumnWidth() in pagelayout type Two Column to configure column widths. documents.t: It is similar to a flexible column. The only difference is that it can only implement the master-detail paradigm up to two pages only. Stack is a layout structure where the required elements show up one by one on a particular action based on the given metadata. Configuration:​ For using the stack layout, select the screenType of pageLayout / PageArea as stack. Example: We have a pageLayout of screentype stack: Stack will render only one layoutSubscreen at a time. As a default, the first layoutSubscreen is rendered. When it is navigated to the second layoutsubscreen it hides the first one & displays the pageArea it is navigated to.

Tab Layout represents a collection of tabs with associated content. The number of tabs rendered will be equal to the number of section/section container ID(s) given in the layout Data section. The tab title will be taken from the section/page Area’s title property, the tab title will only be visible if the flags are maintained in the layout data section and the showTitle property is marked as true. Configuration:​ For using the tab layout, select the screenType of pageLayout / PageArea as tab. In the detail section, mark the showTitle as true. After adding the showTitle as true, in the layout section. For the layouts added (pageArea / section ) add the property showTitle and title, provide the values. Note: selectedKey reflects the currently active tab/section — it is not a one-time "default tab" setting. If bound to a data field, the Tab control will always show whichever tab that field currently holds, and will keep showing it on subsequent loads/refreshes unless the field's value is explicitly reset. If the supplied key doesn't match any tab/section currently rendered, the control falls back to another available tab instead of forcing the configured one. To always land users on the same section regardless of prior state, drive it explicitly through navigation rather than relying on selectedKey alone.

Tree​ The Tree Screen Type is designed to represent hierarchical data in a structured manner. It allows users to visualize relationships between parent and child nodes, making it ideal for displaying nested information such as organisational charts, file systems, or any other hierarchical datasets. Implementation: Data Preparation:​ To prepare the data for a Tree Screen Type, we will use a JSON format that represents the hierarchical structure. Here’s a sample JSON array: [{ "key_01": "value_1", "key_02": "value_2", "key_03": "value_3", "child": [{ "key_01": "value_11", "key_02": "value_22", "key_03": "value_33", "child": [{ "key_01": "value_111", "key_02": "value_222", "key_03": "value_333", "child": [{ "key_01": "value_1111", "key_02": "value_2222", "key_03": "value_3333", }] }] }] }] JSON Structure Each object represents a node in the tree. The child array holds nested objects, representing the child nodes. Key names for child nodes are consistent with parent nodes, ensuring a clear relationship. We will store the data in other type transnode. Screen:​ Step 1: Create one pageArea with screentype, fit_to_area and a section with screentype, tree. In the section layout, add one property autoHeight as true. This ensures that the section dynamically adjusts its height based on the content displayed. Step 2: Create an other type transnode. Step 3: Add Controls for Data Binding Create controls within the section for each key in your JSON data (key_01, key_02, key_03). Bind the section to the other type transnode that contains the hierarchical JSON data. Ensure that each control is correctly bound to the corresponding key in the JSON structure. The Where Used list can be accessed from the context menu of the following elements: Page Page Area Section Transnode To open the Where Used dialog: Right-click on the required element (Page, Page Area, Section, or Transnode). The context menu is displayed. Select Show Where Used from the menu. The Where Used dialog opens, displaying all references for the selected element. When clicking on Show Where Used from the context menu, a Where Used dialog box opens. This dialog displays all references to the selected item within the current application. Dialog Layout​ The Where Used dialog is divided into two sections: **Left Panel (Tree View) ** Displays a hierarchical list of all references for the selected item. **Right Panel (Details View) ** Shows detailed information for the reference selected in the left panel. Selecting an entry in the tree view updates the details shown in the right panel. Supported Elements​ The Where Used feature is available for the following elements: Pages Page Areas Sections Transnodes Reference Checks by Element Type​ **Pages ** The system checks for references in: Application menus Home pages Other pages (including embedded sections and tags) Associated files (controllers, utils) Navigation events within the current page (for example, navTo events) **Page Areas ** The system checks for references in: Associated files(controllers, utils) NavTo Events, layouts in other pages and the current page **Transnodes ** The system checks for references in: Binded data paths Associated files(controllers, utils)

The Where Used dialog allows direct navigation to referenced application objects. In the left tree section, a Navigate button is displayed for application-level objects. Enable permissions for all entities of the application and provide only necessary permissions for the users. Avoid providing all permissions, even if it is an admin user. documents.t: When an entity is created, CRUD permissions are enabled by default. These permissions are available to the TESTER role by default. The permissions are grouped under the default flavor-level permission group: flv_master_grp. Whenever a new flavor is created, the flv_master_grp group is automatically created for that flavor. You can verify these settings under Page Builder → Permission Designer → Permission Groups tab. Select flv_master_grp, then open the Entity Permissions tab to view all CRUD permissions. Refer Permissions - User Guide for detailed explanations. 11.2. Flavor Master Permission(Permissions by default) When a new flavor is created, a master permission group named flv_master_grp is generated by default. This group initially contains only the “TESTER” role by default. To assign default permissions to any additional roles, add them to the flv_master_grp. Within this group, there is a custom permission called flv_master_perm. Any group having the flv_master_perm permission automatically inherits all permissions, regardless of what is configured in the Entity Permissions tab. The flv_master_perm is not exclusive to the flv_master_grp; it can be used in other groups as well, and the behaviour will be the same. Upon entity creation, permissions are automatically assigned to the flv_master_grp for that entity. To disable the impact of flv_master_grp permissions, simply remove all roles from that group. 11.3. Developer permissions Users with the “DEVELOPER” system role have all permissions by default, irrespective of entity-specific configurations.
